title: V13 topics index - 235 rows, one per emitted note, plus a recurs column
description:
## Background
`00 Topics.md` answers *"where did we discuss X"*. It was thrown away during
extraction and is in scope to rebuild.

**The premise that it is a clustered index is FALSE and has been measured.** The
claim that topics "already cluster into ~50 groups of 1-13" does not hold:

| | claimed | **measured** |
|---|---|---|
| groups | ~50 | **225** |
| singletons | — | **221** |
| units sharing a stem with >= 1 other | — | **4 of 235** |
| largest group | 13 | **3** |

A round-3 review measured the same shape independently (212 stems / 199
singletons / max 3 / 13 multi-member groups). The counts differ because the two
normalisers differ; **both agree the claim is false and the maximum is 3.**

The two leading-strip rules originally specified (`nhb - `, `theory - `) match
**0 of 235 topics.** The real boilerplate, measured: `nhb theory` on 108, `nhb
coaching` on 21, `ff guest` on 11, `ff ` on 14, `nhb` on 136 of 230.

**So this is not a clustered index, because there are no clusters. It is a
chronological index with a topic column - 235 rows, 221 of them a single note.**
That is still the right artifact, and still $0.00, but V13 is gated on what
actually exists.

**The population is 235, not 225 and not 344.** 225 is a GROUP count from the
clustering figures; 344 is the count of TARGETS. The 235 is **193 calls + 42
lessons** - the audio units, the same population as `AUDIT.md` and as V12.
`225 - 221 = 4` multi-groups, which must hold `235 - 221 = 9` units, and the same
row said "4 of 235"; the group count is 4 and the units inside them is 9.

## Technical Approach
**One generated note at vault root, linked from `00 Home.md`.** 235 rows, one per
emitted note, plus a `recurs` column. Each row carries ISO date, type, duration
and a wikilink. ~250-400 lines.

**Built by deterministic stem extraction only** - **these rules REPLACE the ones
that matched 0 of 235 units.** In this order, because the order is load-bearing:

1. lowercase, `_` -> space
2. **split on the dash separator FIRST** (`-`, `|`, en/em dash)
3. **drop qualifier segments** - `with|and|part|pt.|feat|featuring ...`. If every
   segment is a qualifier, keep them all.
4. take the last surviving segment as the topic; if it is empty, the head
5. strip the head boilerplate: ordinal, `ff `, `nhb `, then the call-type words
   `guest|speaker|theory|coaching|training|mastermind|mindstream`, then `call`
6. keep only `[a-z0-9 &+]`, collapse spaces, fall back to `untitled`

The subject is frequently the **middle** segment - `nhb coaching call - offer
fundamentals - with kevin sheerin` is a `kevin sheerin`-segment if step 3 is
skipped, and the corpus is full of that shape. **Do not merge stems differing
only by a verb** - `digging into data` and `diving into data` stay separate and
appear adjacent so a human sees the inconsistency once and decides, with the
decision recorded in the script.

**Cost $0.00, ~2 hours**, computed from `clean-names.json` and `scope-final.json`,
both already on disk. No network, no STT, no vendor, no new dependency.

**Two distinct questions, deliberately not conflated.** `00 Topics.md` answers
*"where did we discuss X"*. The per-30-minute transcript headings
(`### 0:00` / `### 0:30`, ~30 min, same $0.00) answer *"where in the call is the
bit about X"* - timestamps already in the utterance data, zero inference,
mechanically verifiable, and it turns every call note into a jumpable outline.
The headings ride on the note, not on the index.

## Success Criteria
- `00 Topics.md` exists at vault root and links only to notes that exist.
- **235 rows, one per emitted note (193 calls + 42 lessons),** each carrying ISO
  date, type, duration and a wikilink, plus a `recurs` column.
- Linked from `00 Home.md`.
- Every stem was produced by the six ordered rules, and the script records the
  decision where two stems were left separate.

## Acceptance Criteria
**Reject a V13 unless it fails on these inputs.** The group clauses were deleted
because they named three different populations and gated a structure measurement
showed does not exist - these tests keep that deletion honest.

- **225 rows or 344 rows** -> reject. 225 is a GROUP count from the clustering
  figures; 344 is the count of TARGETS. The population is **235 = 193 calls + 42
  lessons**, the same population as `AUDIT.md` and as `mp4`. `225 - 221 = 4`
  multi-groups must hold `235 - 221 = 9` units, and the row said "4 of 235" - the
  group count is 4 and the units inside them is 9.
- `nhb coaching call - offer fundamentals - with kevin sheerin` -> the
  `offer fundamentals` segment. Skip step 3 and the corpus's most common shape
  becomes a person's name.
- `digging into data` and `diving into data` -> **two stems**, appearing adjacent
  so a human sees the inconsistency once and decides, with the decision recorded
  in the script. Do not merge stems differing only by a verb.
- An `untitled` stem not produced by the documented fallback -> FAIL, and every
  such fallback is counted.
- **The deleted group clauses reappearing** -> reject outright: "every note under
  `vault/calls/` appears in exactly one topic group", "every group has >= 1 member"
  and "every token in a group heading appears in at least one member's topic
  string" named THREE different populations (193, 344, 235) and gated a structure
  that measurement showed does not exist. **The 235-row re-scope is the live rule.**
- A hand-written heading that no filename supports being emittable -> reject. The
  unforgeable clause survives as a design rule: a stem is derived, never authored.
- **Invert the rule order** and assert the documented 126-unit `untitled` collapse
  is reproduced. If it is not, the implemented order is not the documented order.
- The original leading-strip rules (`nhb - `, `theory - `) -> they match **0 of 235
  topics**. The real boilerplate, measured: `nhb theory` on 108, `nhb coaching` on
  21, `ff guest` on 11, `ff ` on 14, `nhb` on 136 of 230.

**Dependencies.** V13 is the gate over the index note and is downstream of `fzd`,
which builds it from the emitted notes (`a7z`).

**`5ir` now blocks `dgu` (egress), and that edge is CONDITIONAL on the
operator's `00 Topics.md` decision.** Spec §12's mandatory sequence reads
`V13 topics index [CONDITIONAL on the 00 Topics.md decision, §15] -> EMIT the
SHA256 manifest -> ONLY NOW scp -r`, so egress does not run until this gate has
a verdict. The edge exists because the ordering does, not because the graph
decided the content question - §15 records that question as genuinely open
($0.00, ~2.5 h combined with the 30-minute headings, and R4 objects to a vault
without them). The direction is deliberate: the failure mode of a MISSING edge is
"egress runs before V13 validated the index", which ships something unvalidated;
the failure mode of an EXTRA edge is "one bead does not run", which costs a bead.

**If the operator decides `00 Topics.md` is NOT wanted, `br dep rm dgu 5ir` is the
ONLY edge to remove.** Nothing else in the graph changes: `fzd` still builds the
note, `5ir` still gates it, and the other seven egress blockers are untouched.
The P2 -> P1 raise goes with the edge, because that priority exists to keep the
graph and the §12 sequence agreeing.

## Test Plan
- Unit: `nhb coaching call - offer fundamentals - with kevin sheerin` yields the
  `offer fundamentals` segment, not the `kevin sheerin` segment.
- Unit: a stem of `untitled` is only produced by the documented fallback, and
  every such fallback is counted.
- Unit: `digging into data` and `diving into data` remain two stems.
- E2E: build from the emitted notes, assert 235 rows and that every wikilink
  resolves to an existing note.

## Considerations
- **V13's group clauses were DELETED.** An earlier formulation gated "every note
  under `vault/calls/` appears in exactly one topic group", "every group has >= 1
  member" and "every token in a group heading appears in at least one member's
  topic string". Those three named THREE different populations (193, 344, 235)
  and gated a structure that measurement showed does not exist. **The 235-row
  re-scope is the live rule.**
- The unforgeable clause from the deleted formulation survives as a design rule:
  a hand-written heading no filename supports must not be emittable. A stem is
  derived, never authored.
- A per-course, per-year and per-month index tree is NOT in scope. Shipping MOCs
  is optional enrichment and V6's floor is `>= 344` either way; they are not
  counted.
- **The `dgu` edge is conditional and says so where it counts.** It is drawn for
  the spec's sequence, not to settle the content decision. Removing it is a
  one-command act with no other consequence; adding it back is the same. An
  implementer who "tidies" it away on the grounds that Topics.md is undecided
  has just made egress able to run without this gate.
- **This gate is expected to be UNEVALUABLE until the pipeline exists.** A
  specification is not an implementation; a gate is evaluable only once code
  exists that can fail it.
- The formula lives in `stage-1/stage-1-spec.md`. If the two disagree, the SPEC
  wins and this bead is wrong - that is the correct direction of disagreement.

title: Extract 51 OOXML documents with the Python stdlib alone
description:
## Background
51 of the 109 documents are OOXML: **36 docx + 12 pptx + 3 xlsx.** (The other 8
of 109 are 6 txt, 1 png, 1 zip, and 50 are PDFs.) "59 office documents" is
withdrawn - the 8 txt/png/zip files were counted as office.

They unpack with the Python stdlib: **no ffmpeg, no office suite, no vendor, no
new dependency.** Rule 2 is intact - the Ubuntu archive's own packages are not a
paid tier, a metered API, or a vendor's free credit tier.

## Technical Approach
- `.docx` / `.pptx` / `.xlsx` are ZIP containers. `zipfile` + XML parsing.
- Read `word/document.xml`, `ppt/slides/slideN.xml`, `xl/sharedStrings.xml` in
  document order.
- **ZIP+XML, unpacked with the stdlib alone.** Do not add a dependency for this.
- Emit markdown; never emit the source binary.
- **The `Lazy Loading Code` ZIP is 296 MiB and `ElementTree` memory on an 8 GB VM
  is the exposure** - this is the real extraction risk in the documents phase, not
  the 340-page books. **A size-triggered memory guard is mandatory**: enumerate
  members and their uncompressed sizes BEFORE parsing any of them, stream members
  one at a time rather than reading the archive into memory, and fall back to
  `zipfile.ZipFile.open(member)` for any member whose uncompressed size exceeds
  the guard. The ZIP is a member enumeration, not a single read.
- A document that extracts to no text ships as `empty_extraction` with the
  measured facts, never as a fabricated summary and never OCR-billed.

## Success Criteria
- 51 documents extracted, 0 requiring a third-party library.
- Slide and paragraph order preserved.
- Zero `.docx` / `.pptx` / `.xlsx` / `.zip` bytes written to the vault.
- The 296 MiB ZIP is enumerated and its text-bearing members extracted without
  exceeding the memory guard.

## Acceptance Criteria
**Reject an extractor unless it fails on these inputs.**

- **Plant a member whose declared uncompressed size exceeds the guard** and assert
  it is read by streaming (`zipfile.ZipFile.open(member)`) and the peak resident
  set stays bounded. An extraction that works because the guard was never
  exercised has not been tested: the 296 MiB `Lazy Loading Code` ZIP is where
  `ElementTree` memory on an 8 GB VM is the exposure. The ZIP is a **member
  enumeration, not a single read.**
- Any **third-party import** -> reject. Rule 2 is intact: the Ubuntu archive's own
  packages are not a paid tier, a metered API, or a vendor's free credit tier.
- A pptx whose slides come back reordered -> FAIL. A dict iteration that reorders
  slides is silently wrong, and no count assertion catches it.
- A document that extracts to **no text** -> ships `empty_extraction` with the
  measured facts. Reject a fabricated summary and reject an OCR call - none is
  proven free and none is needed.
- Zero `.docx`/`.pptx`/`.xlsx`/`.zip` bytes under `vault/` -> reject otherwise.
- The 51 restated as **59** -> reject. "59 office documents" is withdrawn.
- A ZIP whose central directory disagrees with its member headers -> the central
  directory is authoritative. Enumerate from the directory and never trust a
  filename alone.

**Depends on `0em`** for the document population.

## Test Plan
- Unit: a minimal docx built in-test round-trips to readable markdown.
- Unit: slide order in a pptx survives extraction.
- Unit: a ZIP member whose declared uncompressed size exceeds the guard is read
  by streaming, and the peak resident set stays bounded.
- E2E: all 51 extracted, assert no file outside `markdown`/`text` appears.

## Considerations
- Nothing media-shaped ships. Constraint 1 is absolute and gate V6 enforces it,
  including `docx|pptx|xlsx|csv|zip` in the banned extension set.
- **`attachments/` does NOT exist.** An earlier `VAULT-STRUCTURE.md` mandated it
  holding raw binaries "as fetched" - **that WAS the Constraint 1 violation,
  written into the deliverable by a subordinate document.** Resolved: the binaries
  are fetched, parsed and converted to markdown on the VM, and destroyed with it
  in phase 7. `VAULT-STRUCTURE.md` is explicitly subordinate to the spec, with the
  resolution recorded at the top of it.
- A ZIP's central directory can disagree with its member headers; enumerate from
  the directory and never trust a filename alone.
- **This gate is expected to be UNEVALUABLE until the pipeline exists.** A
  specification is not an implementation; a gate is evaluable only once code
  exists that can fail it.
- The formula lives in `stage-1/stage-1-spec.md`. If the two disagree, the SPEC
  wins and this bead is wrong - that is the correct direction of disagreement.

title: V5 span coverage
description:
## Background
Catches the failure a WPM check cannot: an assembly that **drops the beginning or
the end of a transcript** and still looks plausible in the middle. `WPM_MIN`
catches "too few words overall"; `SPAN_EDGE_SEC` catches "the right number of
words, from the wrong window".

## Technical Approach
```
V5(transcript_words, d_manifest) :=
    head_gap := transcript_words[0].start
    tail_gap := d_manifest - transcript_words[-1].end

    FAIL if transcript_words is empty      # V4 already ensures a duration
    FAIL if head_gap > SPAN_EDGE_SEC       # first minutes of speech missing
    FAIL if tail_gap > SPAN_EDGE_SEC       # last minutes of speech missing
    FAIL if span_ratio < MIN_SPAN_RATIO    # (last_s - first_s) / d_manifest
    PASS otherwise
    NON_VACUOUS iff len(transcript_words) > 0 and d_manifest > 0
```

`SPAN_EDGE_SEC` **read 60 for five review rounds on no evidence.** A census of
**47 units and 94 edges** found the largest edge anywhere is **4.64 s**, so 60 was
**12.9x too loose** - a note missing its first 55 seconds of speech would have
passed the gate whose entire job is to catch that. It is now **10**, which is
2.15x the largest observed and fails 0 of 94 real edges.

**A NEGATIVE gap is NOT a failure and must never be treated as one.** **10 of the
47 units have a negative tail** - the last word ends AFTER the declared duration,
by up to 1.00 s. It is the `pjFQiLQQ` class: the manifest duration is a claim and
the transcript extent is the measurement, so the measurement can exceed the claim.
The formula uses `tail_gap > SPAN_EDGE_SEC`, which a negative value cannot
satisfy, so the case is handled correctly by construction - **stated here because
it is surprising enough that a future reader will otherwise "fix" it.**

**Two failures must be distinguished and they are not the same event.** A unit
with no words is a **fetch or decode failure**; a unit whose words are present but
span too little is an **assembly failure**. The first costs money to retry; the
second means the transcript is being built wrong and retrying will produce the
same wrong answer. Both are FAIL, and they are reported with different names.

## Success Criteria
- V5 PASSES on all 235 units.
- The two failure classes are reported under different names, as above.
- `FAIL if span_ratio < MIN_SPAN_RATIO` is implemented **only once the constant
  has a sourced value** - see the Considerations. Until then the clause is
  recorded as UNSET, not defaulted to 0.

## Acceptance Criteria
**Reject a V5 unless it fails on these inputs.** SPAN_EDGE_SEC read 60 for five
review rounds on no evidence; the largest edge anywhere in a 47-unit, 94-edge
census is 4.64 s, so 60 was 12.9x too loose and a note missing its first 55
seconds of speech passed.

- A transcript whose first word starts at **45 s** of a 4,000 s unit -> FAIL. At
  the withdrawn 60 s this passes; at 10 s it fails. That difference is the whole
  point of the constant.
- A transcript whose last word ends **1.0 s AFTER** `d_manifest` -> **PASS**, not
  FAIL. A negative tail gap is not a failure and an implementation that treats it
  as one fails 10 of the 47 measured units - the `pjFQiLQQ` class, where the
  manifest duration is a claim and the transcript extent is the measurement.
- A transcript with NO words -> FAIL, and reported as a **fetch or decode
  failure**. A transcript with words present spanning only 0.86 of the duration ->
  FAIL, reported as an **assembly failure**. **Both are FAIL and they must carry
  different names** - the first costs money to retry, the second means retrying
  produces the same wrong answer.
- A span_ratio of 0.86 while `MIN_SPAN_RATIO` is UNSET -> the clause must be
  reported **UNSET**, not silently satisfied. A default of 0 makes the clause dead
  while appearing live.
- 234 green units and one unlabelled -> FAIL. V5 spans all 235, and a coverage
  count lower than the population is the same discovery-not-declaration defect.

**Dependencies.** V5's `d_manifest` comes from the submission path (`z72`), whose
`assembled.json` carries the utterance timestamps the gaps are computed from.

## Test Plan
- Unit: a transcript missing its first 30 s -> FAIL.
- Unit: a transcript whose last word ends 1.0 s past `d_manifest` -> **PASS**,
  not FAIL.
- Unit: a transcript with words present but a span_ratio of 0.86 -> FAIL on the
  span clause if and only if `MIN_SPAN_RATIO` is set; the census minimum is
  **0.861794**, so any value below that cannot fail a real unit and any value
  above it fails 1 of 47.
- E2E: all 235; assert zero FAILs and assert the edge distribution is recorded.

## Considerations
- `WPM_MIN = 60` and `WPM_MAX = 300` are also measured, from the same census:
  observed **127.6-251.7 wpm** (42 lessons, all of them, plus 5 calls).
  `WPM_MAX` was **260** and sat only 8.3 wpm above the densest unit with two
  lessons inside 15 wpm of it - one dense lecture from failing a good note.
  300 = 1.19x the densest measured unit, clear of the ~503 a duplicated part
  would produce. `WPM_MIN` at 60 is 47% of the quietest measured unit.
  **Do not widen either bound to make a gate pass.**
- **`MIN_SPAN_RATIO` IS NAMED IN THE SPEC'S FORMULA AND CARRIES NO VALUE
  ANYWHERE.** It appears exactly once, in §11.3's V5, with no entry in §2's
  constants block, no measurement and no provenance - unlike `SPAN_EDGE_SEC`,
  which was measured on 47 units and 94 edges. **Do not invent one.** The census
  artifacts give the observed range - `span_ratio` 0.861794 to 1.000145 over
  `nhbplus-lessons-census-2026-10-15.json` and `nhbplus-call-edges-2026-10-15.json`
  - so a value below 0.8618 cannot fail a real unit and a value above it fails at
  least one of the 47. **This is a gap in the source. Report it, do not fill it.**
- **This gate is expected to be UNEVALUABLE until the pipeline exists.** A
  specification is not an implementation; a gate is evaluable only once code
  exists that can fail it.
- The formula lives in `stage-1/stage-1-spec.md`. If the two disagree, the SPEC
  wins and this bead is wrong - that is the correct direction of disagreement.

title: Remux to .mka with -vn -c:a copy
description:
## Background
This is not a transcode. `ffmpeg -vn -c:a copy` strips the video stream and
copies audio untouched. **137 of 235 fetched primaries are MP4, only 98 are MP3**,
so this is the MAJORITY path, not an edge case. The output container MUST be
`.mka`: `.m4a` is an MP4 container and cannot hold an MP3 elementary stream, so it
fails rc=234 *"Could not write header (incorrect codec parameters)"* for **98 of
235 units**.

The remux is MANDATORY, not an optimisation. Submitting the raw 1,539 MB MP4 of
the corpus's longest call did not complete - it timed out after >1,800 s. The
remuxed 280.7 MB `.mka` of the same audio completed in 105.1 s. Bandwidth was
never the difference: the remuxed file uploaded at 150.8 MB/s, so 1,539 MB is
~10 s of transfer. What differs is that `-vn` strips the h264 video track. Under
Constraint 7 a failed submission is paid and unrecoverable, so this is a
correctness requirement, not a size one.

## Technical Approach
```bash
ffmpeg -nostdin -v error -y -i <source> -vn -c:a copy <part>.mka
```
- `-nostdin` is mandatory. ffmpeg reads stdin by default and will consume the TSV
  driving the loop.
- **`REMUX_CONCURRENCY = 2`. Two `ffmpeg` processes at most, and the number is a
  bound, not a preference.** The compute box is `Standard_D2s_v5` — **2 vCPU**.
  A remux herd is a CPU herd: `-vn -c:a copy` still has to demux, re-timestamp
  and rewrite the container, and it is single-threaded per process. Nothing in
  the pipeline stops an implementer reading `FETCH_CONCURRENCY_CEILING = 38` and
  applying 38 to this step, and **on 2 vCPU that is 19 running processes per
  core**: every remux slows, the loop's own watchdog looks like a stall, and the
  failure presents as a network or vendor problem while the box is simply
  oversubscribed. This is the one concurrency constant in the pipeline that is
  *smaller* than the hardware it runs on, and that is deliberate — the disk cap
  (`06k`) bounds space, this bounds the CPU the remux itself needs.
- **Segment** when a remuxed part reaches `CAP_BYTES = 2,000,000,000` ->
  `ffmpeg -f segment -segment_time SEGMENT_SEC` with `SEGMENT_SEC = 1500`.
  Single-part otherwise. **Every part gets its own receipt entry.** On the measured
  largest unit (402,307,896 B remuxed = 383.7 MiB) it should never fire; if it
  does, that is a finding, not a routine path - log it and report it.
- **Bit-exactness, verified by SHA-256 over decoded PCM:**
  | codec | result |
  |---|---|
  | MP3 | **EXACT**, identical hash over 711 MB and 994 MB of PCM |
  | AAC | near-exact - ~10 KB differs in 1.1 GB (encoder delay on repack) |

  Claim bit-exactness for MP3; claim **near-exact** for AAC. The standing worry
  that a copy codec cannot extract a channel from JOINT-STEREO MP3 was tested and
  is withdrawn: on the corpus's own joint-stereo file it does exactly that,
  losslessly.
- **Size cut - the plan's "~85%" was wrong two ways:**
  | format | units | measured cut | why |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | MP4 | 133 | **+78.5% to +81.8%** | the video track is most of the file |
  | MP3 | 97 | **-1.6% - the output is LARGER** | no video to strip; only repackaging |
  | **corpus** | 235 | **153.81 -> 42.17 GiB (71.2%)** | |

  The real saving is **104.21 GiB, not the 124.43 GiB** an 85% assumption implies.
  `wiUyTRZb` remuxed +1.21% BIGGER, corroborating the negative MP3 cut.
- **Do NOT transcode to 16 kHz PCM.** Measured at **-166% size on MP3** - a
  133.6 MB source becomes 355.9 MB of `s16le`, and 98 of 235 units are MP3. Any
  16 kHz path must use FLAC or Opus, never WAV.
- **`-ac 1 -ar 16000` are OUTPUT options and must follow `-i`.** Placed before it
  they parse as input options and ffmpeg fails *"Option sample_rate not found"*.
  Relatedly, `-v error` suppresses `astats`, which writes at `info` level.

## Success Criteria
- Every part is `.mka`, playable, and Deepgram returns HTTP 200 on it.
- Aggregate output is 71.2% of input, +/- 1 point.
- **Zero re-encode in THIS step.** `-vn -c:a copy` is the only command this bead
  runs. The one permitted re-encode anywhere in the pipeline is the channel
  bead's `EFFECTIVELY_DUAL_MONO` branch, which MUST name `-c:a libopus -b:a 32k,
  mono 16k`. Do not delete that branch by reading this criterion corpus-wide.
- Every part at or above `CAP_BYTES` is segmented, and each segment carries its
  own receipt entry.
- **`REMUX_CONCURRENCY = 2` is enforced by a semaphore around the whole
  remux command, and the bound is asserted, not assumed.** At no point are more
  than two `ffmpeg` processes alive for this step.

## Acceptance Criteria
**Reject a remux implementation unless it fails on these inputs.** The container
choice is a rule, not a preference: `.m4a` fails rc=234 for 98 of 235 units.

- An **MP3 source into `.m4a`** -> FAIL rc=234 *"Could not write header (incorrect
  codec parameters)"*. `.m4a` is an MP4 container and cannot hold an MP3
  elementary stream. A remux that accepts `.m4a` for an MP3 produces 98 broken
  parts, and the error reads like a codec fault when it is not one.
- **SHA-256 over decoded PCM, source vs part, for an MP3** -> equal, over BOTH a
  711 MB and a 994 MB decode. **Assert bytes decoded > 0 first** - SHA-256 of
  nothing equalled SHA-256 of nothing once, and a bit-exactness gate passed on a
  run that checked nothing.
- An **AAC** source -> assert drift < 1 MB per GB and claim **near-exact**, never
  EXACT. ~10 KB differs in 1.1 GB on encoder delay at repack.
- **Any re-encode in this step** -> reject. The only permitted re-encode in the
  whole pipeline is `geo`'s `EFFECTIVELY_DUAL_MONO` branch, and it must name
  `-c:a libopus -b:a 32k, mono 16k`.
- A per-file assertion that the output is SMALLER than the input -> reject. MP3
  gets **LARGER**: `wiUyTRZb` remuxed +1.21% bigger, and 97 of 235 units have a
  **-1.6%** cut. The 71.2% figure is aggregate over the corpus. The real saving is
  **104.21 GiB, not the 124.43 GiB** an 85% assumption implies.
- `-ac 1 -ar 16000` **before** `-i` -> must FAIL (*"Option sample_rate not
  found"*). They are OUTPUT options; placed before `-i` they parse as input
  options. After `-i` they must succeed.
- A 16 kHz PCM (`s16le`) path -> reject. Measured at **-166% size on MP3**: a
  133.6 MB source becomes 355.9 MB, and 98 of 235 units are MP3. Any 16 kHz path
  must use FLAC or Opus, never WAV.
- `ffmpeg` invoked without `-nostdin` -> reject. It reads stdin by default and
  consumes the TSV driving the loop.
- A remuxed part at or above `CAP_BYTES` not segmented, or a segment without its
  own receipt entry -> reject.
- **A remux run that holds more than `REMUX_CONCURRENCY` (2) `ffmpeg` processes at
  once -> reject.** The test is a live process count sampled while the herd runs,
  not a configuration read: an implementation that declares the bound in a
  constant and never applies it to a semaphore is the defect this catches. On a
  2-vCPU `Standard_D2s_v5` a 38-wide herd is 19 processes per core, and the
  symptom is a slowdown that looks like a vendor stall.
- **A remux step with no concurrency bound at all -> reject.** There is nothing in
  the current pipeline that prevents 38 concurrent remuxes, so this is the
  default an implementer will land on unless it is written down. See the
  provenance note in Considerations.

**Depends on `06k`** for the loopback that bounds peak disk while the remux runs,
and on `zyg` for the fetch pool that produces the sources.

## Test Plan
- Unit: SHA-256 over decoded PCM, source vs part, for an MP3 - must be equal.
- Unit: for an AAC source, assert drift < 1 MB per GB.
- Unit: an MP3 source into `.m4a` fails rc=234, proving the container choice is
  the rule and not a preference.
- Unit: `-ac 1 -ar 16000` placed before `-i` fails, and after `-i` succeeds.
- Unit: sample the live `ffmpeg` process count during a remux herd and assert it
  never exceeds `REMUX_CONCURRENCY = 2`.
- Unit (mutation): raise the semaphore width to 38 and assert the process-count
  test above FAILS. A bound whose absence is not detected is not a bound.
- E2E: remux all 235 units, assert 235 `.mka` parts exist and none is `.m4a`.

## Considerations
- MP3 gets LARGER. "71.2% saving" is an aggregate. A per-file expectation that
  every file shrinks will fail on roughly half the MP3 population.
- **`REMUX_CONCURRENCY = 2` has NO PROVENANCE. Spec §2 is titled "Constants -
  every value carries provenance" and this is the only constant in it that
  carries none** — it appears once, at `stage-1/stage-1-spec.md` line 263, with a
  bare `= 2` and no note, while every neighbouring constant is annotated with
  what it was measured from and when. It is nowhere else in the repository: not
  in this bead before this revision, not in any other bead, not in any artifact.
  **It reads like a leftover default, so it must be CONFIRMED, not obeyed.** The
  consequence of 2 is stated above because something must bound the herd and
  this is the only candidate; the value itself is the operator's or a probe's to
  settle, and a probe that measures actual remux wall-clock at 2-way against
  4-way on the `Standard_D2s_v5` settles it in one run at $0.00. Until then this
  bead enforces the bound **and** flags it as unproven, which is the honest
  position.
- **The size guard on the remuxed output is WITHDRAWN, not re-derived.** The old
  "~400 MB against a 2 GiB sentinel" estimate was a display value consumed as a
  threshold, which Constraint 6 forbids, and it was arithmetically inapplicable
  because MP3 has a negative cut. `CAP_BYTES` stays and `SEGMENT_SEC` stays; the
  branch is recorded as never taken.
- The `.mka` container was verified at the vendor for an MP3 source too: a
  5-minute slice of a real corpus MP3 remuxed to `.mka` returned HTTP 200, 911
  words, 300.0 s, for $0.03. Under Constraint 7 an HTTP 400 class there would
  have been 97 paid-and-unrecoverable failures.
- **This gate is expected to be UNEVALUABLE until the pipeline exists.** A
  specification is not an implementation; a gate is evaluable only once code
  exists that can fail it.
- The formula lives in `stage-1/stage-1-spec.md`. If the two disagree, the SPEC
  wins and this bead is wrong - that is the correct direction of disagreement.

title: V8 frontmatter value DOMAINS - not a field count
description:
## Background
Rev 0 asserted a field COUNT, so these all shipped: `duration: 0` on three
units, `speakers: null`, and a `type: mastermind` not in its own vocabulary -
it listed six, not five.

**V8 once parsed a design document instead of the deliverable and passed.** That
is the failure this bead exists to prevent, and it is why `parse_frontmatter`
must read real `---` delimiters from emitted notes and nothing else.

**This bead is the GATE.** Its obligation is that it REJECTS a bad frontmatter
value on sight. `uff` is the EMITTER: it is the code that writes the block. Two
beads, two claims, one shared fixture of six bad inputs — and that is
deliberate. **A pass here proves the validator detects a wrong writer; it does
not prove this pipeline's emitter is correct, and a pass on `uff` does not prove
this gate would catch a wrong emitter.** Neither bead's evidence satisfies the
other's acceptance criteria, which is the point of splitting them.

## Technical Approach
```
V8(notes, scope_final) :=
    for n in notes:
        fm = parse_frontmatter(n)          # REAL --- delimiters
        FAIL if set(fm) != {"date","duration","speakers","type","title"}
        FAIL if not re.match(r"^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$", fm.date) and fm.date != "unknown"
        FAIL if not (fm.duration.isdigit() and int(fm.duration) >= 0)
        FAIL if not (fm.speakers.isdigit()  and int(fm.speakers)  >= 1)
        FAIL if fm.type not in {theory,guest,coaching,training,mastermind,other}
        FAIL if fm.title != Path(n).stem
        FAIL if fm.duration == "0" and word_count == 0    # FLAGGED
    FAIL if any("None" in Path(n).name for n in notes)
    FAIL if any(d.path is None for d in scope_final.documents)
    NON_VACUOUS iff all(fm is not None for fm in fronts) and len(notes) >= 344
```

**The non-vacuity clause is the spec's, verbatim: `all(fm is not None for fm in
fronts)`, not "all parsed".** A `parse_frontmatter` that returns `None` for a note
carrying no `---` block has still "parsed" it, so the weaker wording passes the
exact defect the clause exists to catch: 344 files read, 0 frontmatter parsed,
reported green. `fronts` is the list of `parse_frontmatter(n)` results over
`notes` - the spec names it and never assigns it, so bind it here rather than
paraphrasing the clause into something weaker.
**Provenance of the 344 floor:** spec §11.4 V8, and the measured population
344 = 193 calls + 42 lessons + 109 documents (`pipeline/out/PLAN-TRUTH.json`
`N_TARGETS: 344`; the spec's §10 tree lists 193 + 78 + 37 + 36 = 344 paths plus
`00 Home.md` and `00 Topics.md`).

**The set assertion is `!=`, not a subset test.** A sixth key is a FAIL. The
vocabulary is six values, not five - `mastermind` is one of them and Rev 0's
count-based check rejected a value it had itself listed.

**`duration` is MINUTES, never "3h 14m".** `A2dWSZAK` at `media.dur_s = 50`
(0.833 min, floors to 0) and one unit at 0.0 s whose container reports no duration
at all are both real units, so the lower bound is 0, not 1. An
`integer >= 1` domain **rejects real units in this corpus**; 0 is a truthful minute
count for a sub-minute unit, and the alternative is rounding up, which invents a
second the recording does not have.

**A speaker count is diarisation CLUSTERS, not identified people.** A single
label on a multi-hour call usually means diarisation failed to separate
participants, not that one person spoke. The count is real; the interpretation
is not, and the caveat goes in the note **body**, not a sixth field.

## Success Criteria
- All 344 notes have exactly the five keys.
- **`unknown`, never `null`.** In Obsidian a null frontmatter value renders as
  an empty field, indistinguishable from missing - the absence stops being a
  recorded fact and becomes an omission.
- **`duration: 0` is ALLOWED and is truthful.** 2 of 235 units are sub-minute
  (`A2dWSZAK` at 50 s floors to 0). An `integer >= 1` domain **rejects real
  units in this corpus.** What is not allowed is `duration: 0` WITH zero words -
  that is 50 s of audio transcribing to an empty note, and it is flagged.
- **`V8` parses real `---` frontmatter from the emitted deliverable and nothing
  else.** A gate pointed at a design document is not this gate.
- **`V8` fails on `stage-1/VAULT-STRUCTURE.md`.** That file is the standing
  counter-example; a V8 that returns green on it is reading the wrong subject.

## Acceptance Criteria
**Reject a V8 unless it fails on these inputs.** A V8 that passes any of them is a
field count wearing a domain check's name. Each bullet asserts that `V8(...)`
RETURNS FAIL. `uff` carries the same six inputs as a shared fixture and asserts
the opposite thing — that an emitter never WRITES them. **The shared fixture is
the only thing these two beads share; the claim is not shared.**

- `type: webinar` on an otherwise perfect note -> FAIL. `webinar` is not in the
  six-value vocabulary, and it is the input a count-based check cannot see.
- `duration: 0` **with** `word_count: 0` -> FAIL (flagged). `duration: 0` with
  words present -> PASS. **Both trees are required:** the first is the defect, and
  a V8 that rejects both is too strict by exactly the one real unit in the corpus.
- `fm.date: null` -> FAIL. The domain is `^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$` or `unknown`; a
  null is neither.
- A note with a SIXTH key (`speaker_labels`) -> FAIL on the set assertion. A
  subset test passes it.
- `fm.title` differing from the filename stem by one character -> FAIL.
- A `duration` written as `"3h 14m"` -> FAIL. Minutes only, never a compound
  string.
- A `scope-final.json` whose 37th `written_hand` row has `path: null` -> FAIL,
  naming the document. A silent skip is the defect that stopped the docs shakedown.
- **V8 must parse REAL `---` frontmatter from the emitted notes.** Reject any V8
  whose `parse_frontmatter` reads a design document, a template, or anything
  other than the deliverable's own delimited block. This is the property that
  distinguishes the gate from the emitter: `uff` writes the block, this gate is
  the only thing that proves it was read back.
- **Run V8 against `stage-1/VAULT-STRUCTURE.md`** and assert it FAILS there. That
  is the file V8 once read and passed; if V8 returns green on it, the subject is
  wrong.
- Reject a V8 that reports green over 344 notes where 3 carry `duration: "0"` and
  zero words - the flag must surface, not be absorbed.
- A `speakers` value asserted as identified people -> FAIL. Speaker labels are
  algorithmically derived **clusters**, not people; a single label on a
  multi-hour call usually means diarisation failed to separate participants. The
  caveat belongs in the note **body**, not a sixth field.
- `check-frontmatter.py` counted as V8 -> reject. It reads `VAULT-STRUCTURE.md`,
  not the deliverable. That is a spec-conformance check and its name oversells it.

**Dependencies.** V8 is evaluated over the emitted frontmatter (`uff`) and the
assembled tree (`a7z`), and needs a document `path` from `0em` for all 109.

## Test Plan
- Unit: each of the five domains rejects a bad value and accepts a good one.
- Unit: `duration: 0` with 0 words -> FLAGGED.
- Unit: a `type` outside the six -> rejected.
- Unit: assert `V8` returns FAIL for each of the six shared fixture inputs. The
  assertion is on the RETURN VALUE, not on what an emitter wrote.
- Unit: `V8` pointed at `stage-1/VAULT-STRUCTURE.md` returns FAIL.
- E2E: parse real `---` frontmatter from all 344 emitted notes.

## Considerations
- **The existing `pipeline/scripts/check-frontmatter.py` reads
  `VAULT-STRUCTURE.md`, not the deliverable.** That is a spec-conformance check
  and its name oversells it. It must NOT be counted as V8.
- Speaker count is diarisation CLUSTERS, not identified people. A single label
  on a multi-hour call usually means diarisation failed, not that one person
  spoke.
- **This gate is expected to be UNEVALUABLE until the pipeline exists.** A
  specification is not an implementation; a gate is evaluable only once code
  exists that can fail it.
- **This bead cannot be satisfied by `uff`'s evidence.** An emitter that cannot
  produce six bad values says nothing about whether a validator rejects them;
  the shared fixture is the only thing that transfers between them.
- The formula lives in `stage-1/stage-1-spec.md`. If the two disagree, the SPEC
  wins and this bead is wrong - that is the correct direction of disagreement.

title: Handle the 8 non-OOXML, non-PDF documents
description:
## Background
8 of the 109 documents are neither OOXML nor PDF and were previously unhandled
entirely: **6 `.txt` (including all 5 `Resources Links`), 1 `.png`
(`guNkBLaZ`, 151,552 B, "Pick Primary Color") and 1 `.zip` (`Lazy Loading Code`,
296 MiB).**

## Technical Approach
- Enumerate the class from `scope-final.json` rather than assuming. The eight are
  identified by class, not by name.
- **6 txt** -> stdlib read. **The 5 `Resources Links` need the §10.2 course
  prefix** - they share a stem across 5 courses, and the prefix is what
  disambiguates them (`Million Dollar Branding Resources Links`, `Converting
  Upsells Resources Links`, and so on, each inside its own course folder).
- **1 png** -> **never decoded, never rendered.** Ships as a manifest entry naming
  the file and its dimensions only. It is the one document that collides head-on
  with Constraint 1, and the resolution is that it contributes **no bytes**. Record
  its existence in `_meta/` by description and hash, not by file.
- **1 zip** -> enumerate members, extract text-bearing members via stdlib
  `zipfile`, with a **size-triggered memory guard**. The 296 MiB
  `Lazy Loading Code` ZIP is where `ElementTree` memory on 8 GB is the exposure.
  Enumerate the central directory and member uncompressed sizes BEFORE parsing,
  and stream members one at a time.
- A document that extracts to no text ships as `empty_extraction` with the
  measured facts. **Never OCR-billed** - none is proven free, and none is needed.

## Success Criteria
- All 8 accounted for, each with a declared handling.
- Zero bytes of any image or archive under `vault/`.
- The image is recorded in `_meta/` by description and hash, not by file.
- The 5 `Resources Links` carry a course prefix and land in distinct paths.

## Acceptance Criteria
**Reject a handler unless it fails on these inputs.**

- A `.png` path fed through the exporter that produces a **file** -> reject. It
  must produce a **note**. `guNkBLaZ`, 151,552 B, "Pick Primary Color" is the one
  document that collides head-on with Constraint 1, and the resolution is that it
  contributes **no bytes**.
- The image **omitted entirely** from `_meta/` -> reject. An omission is
  indistinguishable from a loss; a recorded description is not. Record its
  existence by description and hash.
- The ZIP parsed **before** its members are enumerated -> reject. Enumerate the
  central directory and member uncompressed sizes BEFORE parsing, and plant a
  member larger than the guard to prove the guard is live. The 296 MiB
  `Lazy Loading Code` ZIP is where `ElementTree` memory on 8 GB is the exposure.
- Two of the 5 `Resources Links` landing in the **same path** -> reject. They share
  a stem across 5 courses and the course prefix is what disambiguates them.
- A document extracting to no text -> ships `empty_extraction` with the measured
  facts. Reject a fabricated summary and reject an OCR call - none is proven free,
  none is needed.
- `attachments/` present -> reject.
- Any of the 8 identified **by filename** rather than by class from
  `scope-final.json` -> reject. They are identified by class, not by name.

**Depends on `0em`** for the classes and the population.

## Test Plan
- Unit: a `.png` path fed through the exporter produces a note, not a file.
- Unit: V6's banned-extension check catches a planted `.png` in the vault.
- Unit: the ZIP is enumerated before any member is parsed, and the guard is
  exercised by a member larger than the threshold.
- E2E: all 8 handled, assert `vault/` contains no image bytes and no archive.

## Considerations
- `attachments/` does not ship. The document that mandated it is now explicitly
  subordinate to the spec, with the resolution recorded at the top of it.
- Recording the image by description rather than omission is the point: the corpus
  has one image and it must be visible in the audit without being copied. An
  omission is indistinguishable from a loss; a recorded description is not.
- **This gate is expected to be UNEVALUABLE until the pipeline exists.** A
  specification is not an implementation; a gate is evaluable only once code
  exists that can fail it.
- The formula lives in `stage-1/stage-1-spec.md`. If the two disagree, the SPEC
  wins and this bead is wrong - that is the correct direction of disagreement.

title: Generate _meta/AUDIT.md and manifest.json
description:
## Background
Exactly five frontmatter fields carry asserted value domains, and **all
provenance lives in `_meta/manifest.json` plus the generated `_meta/AUDIT.md`** -
never in the notes themselves.

Rev 0 moved every cut fact into `manifest.json` and called it clean. **It is a
relocation.** Obsidian cannot open, search, or link into JSON - every fact the
operator cut from the frontmatter became reachable only by leaving Obsidian and
running `jq`. A cut that moves data into a format the reader's software cannot
open is not a clean cut. **No note gains a field and no note gains a provenance
section; the operator's cut is respected exactly.**

## Technical Approach
- `manifest.json`: every target, its receipt, its SHA-256, its `path`, its
  verbatim MEGA name, and its cost.
- `AUDIT.md` is **GENERATED** from the manifest, never hand-written. A hand-written
  audit is a claim; a generated one is a derivation. ~20 lines of renderer code.
- **`AUDIT.md` is 235 lines, one per audio unit - not 344.** 344 is the count of
  *targets*; only 235 of those are audio units, and V12 clauses 1-4 are all about
  audio units. The 109 documents are verified by §11's path and frontmatter gates,
  not here.
- **Columns, in order:**
  `unit · handle · declared_s · ffprobe_s · settle_s · sha256-12 · verdict`
  **plus `request_id`, RESTORED.** An earlier revision removed the column on the
  strength of "None for EVERY submission"; two later dated artifacts carry a
  non-null value (`syncceiling3`: `01a13ec6-9208-7c90-a68d-0209a8e6be33`,
  `deepgram-eu-limits`: `01a13cfc-1b03-7e10-94cb-a448d81cb512`). Recorded as
  measured, **blank if absent - never invented.**
- Totals in the header, and the file is linked from `00 Home.md`.

## Success Criteria
- `AUDIT.md` regenerates byte-identically from the manifest.
- **235 rows**, one per audio unit, with a `request_id` column present.
- Every cost line reconciles to receipts, and every cost line carries its unit and
  its source artifact.
- No note carries a provenance field.

## Acceptance Criteria
**Reject an AUDIT.md unless it fails on these inputs.** A hand-written audit is a
claim; a generated one is a derivation, and the difference is testable.

- Regenerate **twice** -> byte-identical. Any difference proves the file is
  hand-editable, and the renderer is not a renderer.
- **Alter the manifest** -> the audit changes. A renderer that returns a cached
  value passes an unchanged manifest forever.
- A row count of **344** -> reject. 344 is the count of *targets*; only 235 are
  audio units, and V12's clauses 1-4 are all about audio units. The 109 documents
  are verified by the path and frontmatter gates, not here.
- A `request_id: null` producing the **string "None"** or a crash -> reject. The
  column is present and **blank if absent, never invented**. Two dated artifacts
  carry a non-null value (`syncceiling3`:
  `01a13ec6-9208-7c90-a68d-0209a8e6be33`, `deepgram-eu-limits`:
  `01a13cfc-1b03-7e10-94cb-a448d81cb512`); the column was deleted on the strength
  of "None for EVERY submission", so its absence was a measured claim, not a fact.
- A cost line with no unit and no source artifact -> reject. A figure with its
  unit and its source is a fact; without them it is an anecdote.
- Any note carrying a provenance field or section -> reject. The operator's cut is
  respected exactly.

**Dependencies.** The audit reads V10's settled totals (`c6m`) and V12's identity
binding (`mp4`), and its totals reconcile to receipts.

## Test Plan
- Unit: regenerate twice; assert byte equality, proving it is generated.
- Unit: alter the manifest; assert the audit changes.
- Unit: count the AUDIT rows and assert 235, not 344 - a row-count drift toward
  the target count is the defect this catches.
- Unit: a receipt with `request_id: null` produces a BLANK cell, not the string
  "None" and not a crash.
- E2E: the real manifest and audit.

## Considerations
- **A figure with its unit and its source is a fact; without them it is an
  anecdote.** Every arithmetic claim in this project now carries both, and a
  correction propagates to every cell that cites it.
- An unmarked constant in this project has been a defect every time one was
  found - a forecast below the run it forecasts, a guard that never fires, a
  slack allowance that lets bad data through. **Every one was too permissive.**
- **This gate is expected to be UNEVALUABLE until the pipeline exists.** A
  specification is not an implementation; a gate is evaluable only once code
  exists that can fail it.
- The formula lives in `stage-1/stage-1-spec.md`. If the two disagree, the SPEC
  wins and this bead is wrong - that is the correct direction of disagreement.

title: Assemble the vault tree - 344 notes across four roots
description:
## Background
The deliverable is a markdown vault. Exactly **344 content notes**: `calls/` 193,
`courses/` 78 (42 lesson videos across the **11** structured courses, plus the
36 course_doc files), `written-hands/` 37, `library/` 36. Plus the index notes
`00 Home.md` and `00 Topics.md`.

**Every documented output location needs a `path`.** Rev 0 assigned locations for
the 109 documents that **no artifact actually populated** - `clean-names.json`
carried `handle/verbatim/kind/clean` and **no `path` for any of them**, so V8
failed on its first run and the §9 docs shakedown could not complete.
`design-names.py` now writes a `path` for all 109. Measured: `documents with a
path : 109/109`, `document path collisions : 0`, `total clean paths : 344` =
193 + 42 + 109. **Previously it wrote `path` for calls and lessons and never for a
document.**

## Technical Approach
- Paths come from `pipeline/out/clean-names.json`, which carries **344 measured
  paths**, all unique case-insensitively.
- Never construct a path from a glob or from a title at assembly time.
- `VAULT-STRUCTURE.md` is SUBORDINATE to the spec. Where they disagree the spec
  wins; the resolution table is at the top of that file. **`attachments/` does not
  exist** - it held raw `docx`/`pptx`/`xlsx` "as fetched", which was the
  Constraint 1 violation written into the deliverable by a subordinate document.
- **The 2 sparse PDFs are EXTRACTED, not dropped** (Rule 3). Their note is a
  **stub carrying the measured facts and all 1,372 words verbatim in page order,
  under per-page `#### p. N` headings, with an explicit statement that no layout
  is recoverable.** It is:
  - **not a per-page summary.** At 3.4 words/page the only honest per-page
    artefact is a report of absence, and any actual summary would have to come
    from images - which needs OCR that is not proven free (Rule 2) or fabricates.
    **A summary of an unread page is a fabrication.**
  - **not a reference-only stub.** 1,372 measured characters exist. Discarding
    them is a descope, and Rule 1 forbids it. A bare MEGA handle is the link
    index that stage-0 §1 says this build is not.
  - compatible with Constraint 1: markdown, 0 bytes of media.
- **The single image is recorded by description and hash in `_meta/`, never as a
  file.**
- **Every note carries exactly five frontmatter fields** - `title, date, type,
  duration, speakers` - with asserted value domains, and the speaker-cluster caveat
  in the note **body**, not a sixth field.

## Success Criteria
- 344 notes emitted at exactly the 344 paths in `clean-names.json`.
- Path set equality between what was emitted and what was declared.
- Zero media-shaped bytes anywhere under `vault/`.
- Every one of the 109 documents carries a `path`; zero document path collisions.

## Acceptance Criteria
**Reject an assembly implementation unless it fails on these inputs.**

- Emitting into an **empty tree** then asserting `>= 344` -> FAIL. The floor exists
  so an EMPTY tree cannot read as PASS; that is the trap V6 fell into.
- A document with **no `path`** -> FAIL `7w7`, never silently skip. Rev 0 assigned
  locations for the 109 documents that no artifact actually populated -
  `clean-names.json` carried `handle/verbatim/kind/clean` and **no `path` for any
  of them** - so V8 failed on its first run and the docs shakedown could not
  complete. Measured now: `documents with a path : 109/109`, `document path
  collisions : 0`, `total clean paths : 344`.
- A **346-note flawless run** -> PASS. Reject an implementation asserting `== 344`;
  the spec's own tree also names `00 Home.md` and `00 Topics.md`.
- A path constructed at assembly time from a **glob or a title** -> reject. Paths
  come from `pipeline/out/clean-names.json`, which carries 344 measured paths, all
  unique case-insensitively.
- The **2 sparse PDFs** must ship as stub notes carrying the measured facts and
  **all 1,372 words verbatim in page order, under per-page `#### p. N` headings,
  with an explicit statement that no layout is recoverable.** Reject a per-page
  summary - a summary of an unread page is a fabrication. Reject a reference-only
  stub - 1,372 measured characters exist and discarding them is a descope under
  Rule 1.
- The corpus's **only image** must contribute **no bytes** while still being
  visible in the audit. Reject any route that ships page screenshots: that is
  exactly the shortcut that exists to stop someone doing this.
- `attachments/` present -> reject. It held raw `docx`/`pptx`/`xlsx` "as fetched",
  which was the Constraint 1 violation written into the deliverable's structure by
  a subordinate document.
- A note carrying a **sixth frontmatter field** -> reject. The speaker-cluster
  caveat goes in the note body.

**Dependencies.** Assembly consumes the transcript from `z72` and the three
document extractors (`5zb`, `dqh`, `8pt`). Every gate downstream is evaluated over
what this bead emits.

## Test Plan
- Unit: every declared path's parent directory is created.
- Unit: emitting into an empty tree then asserting `>= 344` - the floor exists so
  an EMPTY tree cannot read as PASS.
- Unit: a document with no `path` fails V8, not silently skips.
- E2E: assemble from clean-names, assert set equality with the 344.

## Considerations

- `Resources Links` is the stem shared by 5 files. They are disambiguated by the

- **The corpus's only image collides head-on with Constraint 1**, and the
  resolution is that it contributes **no bytes** while still being visible in the
  audit. The route Constraint 1 *blocks* - page screenshots so a human can read the
  book in Obsidian - is exactly the shortcut that exists to stop someone doing

title: V10 the spend gate - same settle quantity as the submission path
description:
## Background
One stop: **`SPEND_HARD_STOP_USD = $213.48`**, DERIVED from
`(34,472.10 + 294.84 + 1,569.62) min x $0.0056 = $203.48`, plus a `$10.00` loss
reserve.

**That constant carried four different values at once** - $207.31 (the budget
artifact), $207.35 (the spec, twice), $207.68 (labelled "DERIVED, not asserted")
and $203.48 - and the block that insisted it was "DERIVED, not asserted" was
itself the wrong one. **A constant that carries four values and a paragraph
insisting it is derived rather than asserted is a constant nobody can stop the run
against.** The live value is $213.48 and `pipeline/out/PLAN-TRUTH.json` carries
`STOP: 213.48`. **Quote ONE value.**

**$200 < $213.48, so the vendor's own 402 backstop fires BEFORE our gate.** The
402 is a backstop at $200 per account, not a ceiling at $213.48 - round 2 caught
that "strictly stronger" was backwards. Two accounts are required and the ledger
is per-account.

## Technical Approach
```
V10(receipts) :=
    # SETTLE_FROM is defined once and used twice, identically:
    #     settle = duration_seconds x INPUT_CHANNEL_COUNT
    # NOT the response's channel array - Deepgram returns channels=1 for a
    # stereo input WHILE BILLING 2x.
    # NOT the pre-downmix part - the BIT_IDENTICAL branch re-runs -map_channel
    # and produces a MONO part, so reading the pre-downmix count settles every
    # downmixed unit at 2x and double-counts the saving.

    committed = sum(COMMIT_COST(r) for r in receipts if r.state == "settled")
    total      = committed + LOSS_ALLOWANCE_USD
    FAIL if total > SPEND_HARD_STOP_USD
    FAIL if any(r.settle_quantity is None for r in receipts)

    # PAID_UNKNOWN counts AGAINST the stop. It is money already spent whose
    # amount is unknown. Excluding it would make the gate pass by not knowing.
    total_including_unknown = total + sum(
        upper_bound(r) for r in receipts if r.state == "PAID_UNKNOWN")

    NON_VACUOUS iff len(receipts) > 0 and
                   committed > 0 and
                   every(r.settle_quantity == settle_from(r) for r in receipts)
```

**`COMMIT_COST` is the only route from seconds to dollars, and it divides by 60:**

```
COMMIT_COST = (billed_seconds(part) / 60) * (RATE + KEYTERM_RATE)
              RATE_USD_PER_MIN = 0.0043 ; KEYTERM_RATE = 0.0013 -> 0.0056
```

`RATE` and `KEYTERM_RATE` are USD PER MINUTE while `billed_seconds` is SECONDS.
Without the `/60` a 3,600 s part commits $20.16 instead of $0.336 and the corpus
commits $11,764.40 instead of $196.07 - a **60x OVERCOMMIT** that would stop the
run after roughly ten parts. This is the same unit slip that produced the 273.7x
error.

**`billed_seconds` is the DECODED PCM length, never a container header.**
`pjFQiLQQ`'s header claims 4,958.7 s while its decoded PCM is 5,431.8 s
(**+9.54%**); a header-derived reservation is under-reserved by exactly the
header's error, per part, silently. The gap is per-file, not a corpus-wide
constant - `wiUyTRZb` agrees to 1 ms - so a correction measured on one unit does
not transfer to another.

**`LOSS_ALLOWANCE_USD = 10.00`**, 5% of ~235 units at the mean COMMIT_COST $0.86 =
$9.89. It is a rounding reserve, not a contingency for a bad estimate, and it
leaves 1.1% headroom, which is marginal and is stated as marginal.

## Success Criteria
- Committed spend never exceeds **$213.48**, summed over BOTH accounts.
- `PAID_UNKNOWN` counts **AGAINST** the stop at its upper bound. Excluding it
  makes the gate pass by not knowing.
- Every receipt's stored `settle_quantity` equals a fresh `settle_from(r)`.
  Divergence FAILS the gate.
- The stop is held against the keep-stereo ceilings, not re-derived from a share:
  **$193.04** if every dated call keeps 2 channels, **$201.83** across all 235
  units.

## Acceptance Criteria
**Reject a V10 unless it fails on these inputs.** A success-only spend counter
sails past a 504 storm; these are the inputs that catch it.

- A receipts set in which one part's stored `settle_quantity` is `null` -> FAIL.
  The clause is `FAIL if any(r.settle_quantity is None for r in receipts)`, and an
  implementation that defaults it to 0 passes the set.
- **Two required runs, not one:** a set whose total is $213.47 must PASS and the
  same set plus a `PAID_UNKNOWN` part carrying a $1.00 upper bound must FAIL. A
  V10 that has never passed anything has not been shown to be able to.
- A primary at $205.00 and a secondary at $8.00 -> FAIL **on the primary's own
  total**, even though the sum ($213.00) is under the stop. The ledger is
  per-account and the 402 backstop fires at $200 per account, so a sum-only
  implementation is blind to the account that is about to be cut off.
- A stereo part whose response carries `channels=1` -> the receipt's
  `INPUT_CHANNEL_COUNT` must be 2 and the settle must be 2x. A V10 that reads the
  response's channel array settles every stereo unit at 1x and lands $193 under
  where it should be.
- A BIT_IDENTICAL part that was downmixed -> settle at **1x, not 2x**. Reading the
  pre-downmix count double-counts the saving.
- A 3,600 s part -> commits **$0.336, not $20.16**. The `/60` is load-bearing;
  without it the corpus commits $11,764.40 instead of $196.07, a 60x OVERCOMMIT
  that would stop the run after roughly ten parts.
- `bin/rescan.py` replayed over the lessons census receipts -> **$8.79 to the
  cent.** A ledger that disagrees with its own receipts is rejected; receipts win,
  and the ledger is the thing that is wrong.

**Dependencies.** V10 reads the ledger (`md5`), settles from receipts written by
`z72`, and is asserted against the test harness (`emn`).

## Test Plan
- Unit: a stereo part with `INPUT_CHANNEL_COUNT == 2` settles at 2x even though
  the response says 1 channel object.
- Unit: a BIT_IDENTICAL part that was downmixed settles at 1x, not 2x.
- Unit: a receipt whose stored quantity differs from `settle_from` -> FAIL.
- Unit: a 3,600 s part commits **$0.336, not $20.16** - the `/60` assertion, run
  explicitly and loudly.
- E2E: replay the lessons census receipts; assert the total is **$8.79** to the
  cent.

## Considerations
- The loss reserve is $10.00 = 5% of ~235 units at the mean $0.86 ($9.89).
- `INPUT_CHANNEL_COUNT` is recorded in the SAME atomic write as `sent`.
- **The share is still SAMPLED at 65 of 191, not censused.** The census exists
  only to PRICE the budget and VALIDATE the ceiling before the run starts; the run
  replaces it with a measurement, because the channel count is read on every file
  as part of a step the pipeline performs anyway. **The residual risk is bounded by
  construction rather than by sample size.**
- **A success-only spend counter sails past a 504 storm.** Rev 0 counted only what
  succeeded; the correct counter includes `lost` and `PAID_UNKNOWN`.
- **This gate is expected to be UNEVALUABLE until the pipeline exists.** A
  specification is not an implementation; a gate is evaluable only once code
  exists that can fail it.
- The formula lives in `stage-1/stage-1-spec.md`. If the two disagree, the SPEC
  wins and this bead is wrong - that is the correct direction of disagreement.

title: V3 STT contracts - one sync path, sent-before-socket
description:
## Background
There is exactly one submission path; the async branch was **deleted**, not
deferred. Ordering is the contract: `sent` is persisted BEFORE the socket opens,
because a process death between submit and record leaves the money spent and
nothing on disk to prove it.

**Rev 0's resume rule could not distinguish a kill before the socket opened from
a kill mid-request, and therefore re-billed.** "Resume never re-bills" was
asserted while the state machine was blind to the one bit that decides it. V3 is
the gate that asserts the ordering holds, and it is the only place the contract
is checked rather than assumed.

## Technical Approach
```
V3(parts, receipts) :=
    FAIL if any(r.transport != "sync" for r in receipts)
    # there is no async path. 7.2 deleted it. A receipt naming an async job is
    # a receipt from a plan that no longer exists.
    for r in receipts:
        FAIL if not r.has("sent") or not r.has("http_status")
        FAIL if r.sent_ts >= r.socket_open_ts     # inverted = contract broken
    FAIL if any(r.http_status != 200 for r in receipts)
    FAIL if any(not r.response_complete for r in receipts)
    NON_VACUOUS iff len(receipts) > 0
```
**Both `http_status == 200` AND `response_complete` are required.** A 200 with
`response_complete` false is a truncated file, not a transcript.

**`PAID_UNKNOWN`, never a clean zero.** A `queued` part was never sent: not
settled, not counted in `committed`, not `PAID_UNKNOWN`. A `sent` part with no
response **is** `PAID_UNKNOWN` and is never auto-resubmitted - the operator
decides. This branch table is in the `kgb` bead; V3 asserts it holds.

**`sent_ts >= socket_open_ts`, not `!=`.** Equal timestamps are the defect: a
clock with one-second granularity records both events in the same second, and a
`!=` comparison passes a pair that never established an ordering.

## Success Criteria
- No receipt names an async transport.
- `sent_ts < socket_open_ts` on every receipt.
- A truncated response fails V3 even with HTTP 200.

## Acceptance Criteria
**Reject a V3 unless it fails on these inputs.** The async branch was measured
away - a 2-min clip and a 68-min clip both return inline results with
`request_id` None - so an implementation that still permits one is a defect with
no evidence behind it.

- A receipt with `transport: "async"` -> FAIL. A receipt naming an async job is a
  receipt from a plan that no longer exists.
- A receipt with `sent_ts > socket_open_ts` -> FAIL. **And a receipt with the two
  timestamps EQUAL** -> FAIL. A `!=` comparator passes equal timestamps, and equal
  timestamps prove nothing about ordering.
- HTTP 200 with `response_complete: false` -> FAIL. The body is a truncated file.
- `http_status` absent from a `sent` receipt -> FAIL. Without it a 504 body, a 429
  body and a 402 body are all "a response", and the state machine settled a 504 as
  a completed transcription once.
- **An empty receipts list** -> FAIL, not PASS. `NON_VACUOUS iff len(receipts) > 0`
  and a V3 that goes green over zero receipts has evaluated nothing.
- Kill the process between the `sent` write and the socket open, restart, and
  assert the part reads `PAID_UNKNOWN` - **never `queued` and never re-submitted.**

**Dependencies.** V3 asserts the ordering the `kgb` state machine implements and
is evaluated over receipts produced by `z72`.

## Test Plan
- Unit: a receipt with `sent_ts > socket_open_ts` -> FAIL.
- Unit: HTTP 200 with `response_complete: false` -> FAIL.
- E2E: kill between `sent` and socket open; on restart the part is
  `PAID_UNKNOWN`, never `queued`.

## Considerations
- A receipt naming an async job is a receipt from a plan that no longer exists.
- `PAID_UNKNOWN` is money spent whose amount is unknown. It is never
  auto-resubmitted.
- **This gate is expected to be UNEVALUABLE until the pipeline exists.** A
  specification is not an implementation; a gate is evaluable only once code
  exists that can fail it.
- The formula lives in `stage-1/stage-1-spec.md`. If the two disagree, the SPEC
  wins and this bead is wrong - that is the correct direction of disagreement.

title: Egress - binary-only copy of vault/ and _meta/ to the PC, V6 before the copy
description:
## Background
The finished markdown IS the deliverable and lands on the operator's PC. Nothing
media-shaped ever does. Constraint 1 is absolute and V6 enforces it - and **V6
must run on the VM source tree BEFORE the copy**, because once a media file lands
on the operator's PC, Constraint 1 has already been violated.

W0-Egress planted a `.mp3` in the source tree and `scp` copied it to the PC.
**The transfer is a dumb binary pipe with no filter, and that is correct.** The
control does not belong there: **a gate placed downstream of an irreversible step
reports a breach that already happened.** V6 must sit upstream of the only
irreversible action in the pipeline.

## Technical Approach
Binary-only copy of `vault/` + `_meta/`. **No PowerShell pipeline.** W0-Egress
proved they corrupt typography: 11 of 11 spot-checks differed while 256 matched on
length. **Length is not integrity.** The two forbidden rewrites are
`Get-Content -Raw | Set-Content -Encoding utf8` and piping a file through a
`python -c` heredoc - both corrupt non-ASCII.

**The mandatory sequence, and the ordering is load-bearing:**

```
assemble vault/
  -> V6  on the VM, zero media extensions and stems   <-- BEFORE any transfer
  -> V7  reduction diff, re-render byte-compare
  -> V8  frontmatter value domains + every document has a path
  -> V9  counts, and EVERY audio target handle has exactly one note
        scope-final.json's kinds are audio/written_hand/course_doc/orphan_doc.
        There is NO kind == "call": the old matcher hit 0 handles and PASSED
        VACUOUSLY on the very call the gate exists to catch.
  -> V10 settled + lost <= hard stop, from receipts
  -> V12 identity binding
  -> V13 topics index
  -> EMIT the SHA256 manifest of vault/ + _meta/   (no step produced this before)
  -> ONLY NOW  scp -r VM -> PC
  -> V11 SHA256 compare on the PC
```

**Egress is always PC-initiated.** The SSH key lives on the PC, so running `scp`
from the VM fails on host resolution: `rc=255 "Could not resolve hostname c"`,
which reads like a network fault and is not one.

**`copy-verification.json` schema, fixed so phase 6 cannot be skipped by
omission:**

```
copy-verification.json = {
  "generated": ISO-8601,
  "source": "VM:/data/nhb/vault",
  "files": [ {"relpath": str, "bytes": int, "sha256": hex64} ],   # every file
  "notes_expected": 344, "notes_found": int,   # 344 = 193 calls + 42 lessons
                                                # + 109 docs. + 00 Home.md
                                                # + 00 Topics.md if the index
                                                # notes ship. See V6.
  "typography_checked": int, "typography_passed": int
}
```

The destroy step comes only after verification. It is the one irreversible action
in the pipeline.

## Success Criteria
- `vault/` and `_meta/` present on the PC, byte-identical.
- `copy-verification.json` written, matching the schema above, and every hash
  matching.
- Zero media-shaped bytes on the PC side.
- Every gate in the sequence above is recorded green, in order, before `scp` runs.

## Acceptance Criteria
**Reject an egress step unless it fails on these inputs.** The transfer is a dumb
binary pipe with no filter, and that is correct - the control belongs upstream of
the irreversible step.

- **Delete the manifest step** from the sequence and assert the run **REFUSES** to
  reach `scp`. A run that reaches `scp` without a file manifest emitted by an
  earlier step is rejected. No step produced that manifest before this bead.
- Plant a `.mp3` in the VM source tree and run the sequence -> V6 must FAIL the run
  **before** the transfer. W0-Egress proved `scp -r` copied a planted `.mp3`
  faithfully. A V6 wired downstream of the copy reports a breach that already
  happened.
- Rewrite one copied file with `Get-Content -Raw | Set-Content -Encoding utf8` ->
  V11 must FAIL. The two forbidden rewrites are that and piping a file through a
  `python -c` heredoc; both corrupt non-ASCII. W0-Egress measured 11 of 11
  spot-checks differing while 256 matched on length.
- A `copy-verification.json` written **after** `scp` rather than before -> reject.
  A copy verified only after the source is destroyed is a copy that cannot be
  verified. Phase 6 exists precisely so that cannot happen by omission.
- `notes_found != notes_expected` in the schema -> FAIL.
- `scp` launched **from the VM** -> reject. Egress is always PC-initiated because
  the SSH key lives on the PC; running it from the VM fails on host resolution
  with `rc=255 "Could not resolve hostname c"`, which reads like a network fault
  and is not one.
- Reject a filter added to `scp -r`. Do not add a filter to it and do not rely on
  it to be one; put the control where it can still stop the step.

**Dependencies.** This bead runs V6 (`okr`), V7 (`pgs`), V8 (`7w7`), V9 (`wl2`),
V10 (`c6m`), V12 (`mp4`) and V13 (`5ir`), and emits the SHA-256 manifest that
`9zh` and `r0k` consume.

**All seven now have a path, and five are direct edges.** `dgu` blocks on `okr`,
`pgs`, `7w7`, `wl2` and `5ir` directly. `c6m` (V10) and `mp4` (V12) reach it
transitively through `9zh`, which is deliberate: §12's sequence is
`V10 -> V12 -> EMIT the SHA256 manifest -> ONLY NOW scp -r`, and §12.1's phase-4
gate for the audit row is "V12 clause 4", so the manifest emitter is the right
thing for them to block on. V7 (`pgs`) and V13 (`5ir`) were added here because
the sequence names them and neither had any path to egress at all - `pgs` had no
dependents whatsoever, so V7 could fail while the copy ran.

**The `5ir` edge is CONDITIONAL on the operator's `00 Topics.md` decision**
(§15, still open: $0.00, ~2.5 h combined with the 30-minute transcript
headings, and R4 objects to a vault without them). It is drawn for the spec's
sequence, not to settle a content question the operator has not answered. The
failure mode of a MISSING edge is "egress runs before V13 validated the index",
which ships something unvalidated; the failure mode of an EXTRA edge is "one
bead does not run", which costs a bead. **If the operator decides `00 Topics.md`
is NOT wanted, `br dep rm dgu 5ir` is the ONLY edge to remove**, and the
P2 -> P1 priority raises on `5ir` and `fzd` go with it.

## Test Plan
- Unit: `vault/` passes V6 on the VM BEFORE the copy starts.
- Unit: the file manifest is emitted by a step that ran before `scp`; a run that
  reaches `scp` without one is refused.
- Unit: a planted `.mp3` in the VM source tree fails V6 and stops the sequence
  before the transfer.
- Unit: **each of `pgs` and `5ir` failing** stops the sequence before `scp`. Both
  were reported green-less than once: `pgs` had no dependents at all, so a V7
  failure could not stop anything, and `5ir` had no path to egress either.
- E2E: copy, then V11 on the PC side, and assert `notes_found == notes_expected`.

## Considerations
- A copy that is verified only after the source is destroyed is a copy that cannot
  be verified. **Order is load-bearing.**
- `scp -r` copies whatever it is given. Do not add a filter to it and do not rely
  on it to be one; put the control where it can still stop the step.
- **A gate with no dependents is a gate that cannot stop anything.** That is the
  same defect class as a gate that cannot fail, one level up: V7 once sat in
  this sequence's prose with no edge behind it, so its verdict reached nothing.
- **This gate is expected to be UNEVALUABLE until the pipeline exists.** A
  specification is not an implementation; a gate is evaluable only once code
  exists that can fail it.
- The formula lives in `stage-1/stage-1-spec.md`. If the two disagree, the SPEC
  wins and this bead is wrong - that is the correct direction of disagreement.


Dependencies:
  -> nhbplus-corpus-wl2 (blocks) - V9 counts AND one-note-per-call, with the vacuity that hid a defect
  -> nhbplus-corpus-7w7 (blocks) - V8 frontmatter value DOMAINS - not a field count
  -> nhbplus-corpus-pgs (blocks) - V7 reduction diff - the vault is a pure function of receipts
  -> nhbplus-corpus-okr (blocks) - V6 nothing media-shaped under vault/ - and a floor
  -> nhbplus-corpus-yx4 (blocks) - Build the source-document archive - beside vault/, never inside
  -> nhbplus-corpus-9zh (blocks) - Generate _meta/AUDIT.md and manifest.json
  -> nhbplus-corpus-5ir (blocks) - V13 topics index - 235 rows, one per emitted note, plus a recurs column

Dependents:
  <- nhbplus-corpus-r0k (blocks) - V11 egress SHA256 per file

## The source archive is in scope for this bead

Egress copies **three** things, not two: `vault/`, `_meta/`, and
`nhbplus-source-documents.zip`. The archive sits **beside** the vault, never
inside it, which is why V6 needs no change — it scans `vault_dir` and the
archive is not in it. **Emit the SHA-256 manifest over all three**, and
carry the archive into `copy-verification.json`'s file list and byte
comparison. An egress that transfers the vault and forgets the archive
delivers a deliverable that cannot answer *"where did this note come from?"*.

title: Extract 50 PDFs with pypdf - 48 text, 2 sparse, 0 raster
description:
## Background
Documents are processed BEFORE the paid pipeline: a free end-to-end shakedown of
fetch, extract, render, assemble and egress. **109 documents = 37 written_hand +
36 course_doc + 36 orphan.** Of the 109, **50 are PDFs**, 51 are OOXML (36 docx +
12 pptx + 3 xlsx) and 8 are txt/png/zip.

**`48 text + 2 sparse + 0 raster = 50`, and the gate is closed on 50 of 50.**
An earlier artifact reported `47 + 2 + 0` against its own declared `total: 50` -
**the parts did not sum to the total, and the run printed a confident summary
table anyway.** The document missing from that reclassification was
`6. 7-Figure VSL Script Template`, dropped by a hand-typed target list missing
its `6. ` ordinal and swallowed by `if not r: continue`. **The 48 was correct and
the artifact was incomplete. Both are now true at once.** Do not carry the 47.

## Technical Approach
```python
# pypdf 4.0.2, Ubuntu 24.04 archive (python3-pypdf 4.0.2-1). Not pip, not a vendor,
# no account, no egress. Rule 2 is intact: a distro package is none of the
# forbidden categories.
page.extract_text(visitor_text=...)   # per-span font size, baseline, x
```
- **REJECTED:** content-stream `Tj`/`TJ` regex. It yields hex glyph indices, not
  characters - a raster page scored **449,418 "characters"** and 597/597 "pages
  with text" that way. Character count is not a text-layer test.
- **Images are enumerated via `/Resources /XObject` and NEVER decoded. 0 bytes
  written** across the whole run.
- **Calibration, re-measured on this corpus - do not inherit the skill's values:**
  ```
  Y_TOL    = 0.6   Digest-stable on 48 of 50: SHA-256 of the ordered line TEXTS
                  is byte-identical at 0.0 / 0.25 / 0.5 / 0.6 / 1.0 / 2.0 / 3.0 /
                  5.0 pt. Geometry moves (baselines 444 -> 128 on the 22-page
                  Swipe document); text does not.
                  LOAD-BEARING on 2 documents, whose baselines sit within a few
                  points of each other: "500-page-swipe-file-clayton-makepeace_compress_1.pdf"
                  and "fourdaycashmachine.pdf". Both are 1.0pt documents.
                  Recorded as a known non-uniformity, not smoothed over.
  TIER_MIN = 5     A tier is a size carried by >= 5 lines. Populations on the
                  22-page document are 395 / 133 / 11, so T in 2..10 all recover
                  the same tiers. T=5 tolerates a stray span that T=2 would
                  promote to a tier.
  TIER RULE= gate first, then title = largest tier, body = most frequent tier,
                  every OTHER tier = a heading tier.
                  Measured on Swipe: title 60.0pt, headings [24.0pt] over 133
                  lines (25% of 539), body 11.04pt.
  DEGENERATE_PT = 2.0   the gate. A dominant font at or below 2.0pt files the
                  document as degenerate_geometry. This is the actual rule, and
                  it is a FONT-SIZE gate, NOT a words-per-page threshold.
  ```
  Inherited constants rejected: the skill's flat `18.0pt` (this corpus tiers
  60 / 24 / 11.04), and `title_size x 0.55` -> **33.0pt, which silently excludes
  the 24.0pt heading tier** - that is what made an early extractor report
  `headings=0` on a document carrying 133.

| class | count | handling |
|---|---|---|
| `text` | **48** | tiering and reflow valid |
| `sparse` | **2** | *AC eBook*, *AC_Book* - 340 pp each, `page_cap: 200`. See §8.2. |
| `raster` | **0** | would ship `empty_extraction` and never be OCR-billed |

**65,985 recoverable words**, and the parts account for every one of them:
`already_text` 42,683 + `recovered_text` 21,930 + `sparse_text` 1,372 +
`raster` 0 = **65,985**. Zero documents require OCR.

**Links: `/Annots` is the ONLY authoritative link layer.** *Swipe* carries 400
raw annotations, **201 distinct** - half are boilerplate repeats. The text layer's
copy of those URLs is MANGLED by line wrapping (a Google Sheets link renders as
`...acQ/e` then `dit#gid=5683798` on the next baseline, and `Calculator` tears to
`Calcu` / `dit#gid=...` / `lator`). **Never recover a URL from display text.**

**The page cap.** `page_cap: 200`, and THREE of 50 PDFs hit it - not two:

| document | pages read | never opened | words |
|---|---|---|---|
| `2. AC eBook` | 200/340 | 140 | 691 |
| `500-page-swipe-file-clayton-makepeace_compress_1` | **200/597** | **397** | **20,205** |
| `AC_Book` | 200/340 | 140 | 681 |

**677 of their 1,277 pages - 53.0% - are never opened, and they carry 21,577
words, which is 32.7% of every word in the PDF half of the corpus.**
`500-page-swipe-file-clayton-makepeace_compress_1` is the single largest document
in the set by words and the one most damaged by the cap. Raising the cap is a
decision, not an oversight: at 101 words/page the remaining 397 pages are ~40,000
words, about 60% more text than the whole PDF half currently yields. Cost: zero -
pypdf is installed and extraction is local. The spec ships `page_cap: 200`; the
number is recorded so the choice can be revisited with it in hand.

## Success Criteria
- 50 PDFs processed, 0 fetch failures, $0.00.
- Class counts are **48 / 2 / 0** and **sum to 50**. An audit asserts
  `parts == total` before it writes.
- Word total is 65,985 and the per-document parts sum to it.
- Zero image bytes decoded, zero paid API calls.
- Each of the three page-capped documents is identified **by name**, and its
  `pages_read` / `pages_total` / word count is recorded in `_meta/`.
- Every URL written into a note came from `/Annots`, never from display text.

## Acceptance Criteria
