**Reject a PDF extractor unless it fails on these inputs.** The parts did not sum
to the total once and the run printed a confident summary table anyway.

- A classification audit whose parts do not equal its own declared total -> FAIL
  before it writes. `47 + 2 + 0` against `total: 50` shipped once.
- The document missing from that reclassification - `6. 7-Figure VSL Script
  Template` - must be present. It was dropped by a hand-typed target list missing
  its `6. ` ordinal and swallowed by `if not r: continue`. **The 48 was correct
  and the artifact was incomplete; both are true at once.** Do not carry the 47.
- A degeneracy gate keyed on **words per page** -> reject. The actual rule is
  `DEGENERATE_PT = 2.0`, a FONT-SIZE gate. The invented `>= 10 words/page`
  classifier appears in no artifact and misfiles THREE real documents as sparse -
  and `7-Figure VSL Script Template` **measured 814 words/page on one page, 80x
  the sparse threshold.** It is the least sparse document in the set.
- A 7-words-per-page document with an 11.04pt dominant font -> classed **`text`**,
  not `sparse`.
- A hex-glyph content stream (`Tj`/`TJ` regex) -> yields **no words**. A raster
  page scored **449,418 "characters"** and 597/597 "pages with text" that way.
  Character count is not a text-layer test.
- Zero image bytes decoded, across the whole run. Images are enumerated via
  `/Resources /XObject` and never decoded.
- **A URL recovered from display text** -> reject. `/Annots` is the ONLY
  authoritative link layer. *Swipe* carries 400 raw annotations, 201 distinct; the
  text layer's copy is mangled by line wrapping - a Google Sheets link renders as
  `...acQ/e` then `dit#gid=5683798` on the next baseline, and `Calculator` tears to
  `Calcu` / `dit#gid=...` / `lator`.
- `Y_TOL` digest equality at 0.0 / 0.25 / 0.5 / 0.6 / 1.0 / 2.0 / 3.0 / 5.0 pt on
  the 22-page Swipe document -> the ordered line TEXTS hash byte-identically at all
  eight. It is LOAD-BEARING on 2 documents whose baselines sit within a few points
  of each other. Recorded as a known non-uniformity, not smoothed over.
- The three page-capped documents named: `2. AC eBook` (200/340, 691 words),
  `500-page-swipe-file-clayton-makepeace_compress_1` (**200/597, 20,205 words**),
  `AC_Book` (200/340, 681 words). **677 of their 1,277 pages - 53.0% - are never
  opened, and they carry 21,577 words, which is 32.7% of every word in the PDF
  half.**
- A word total that is not **65,985** with the parts summing to it
  (`already_text` 42,683 + `recovered_text` 21,930 + `sparse_text` 1,372 +
  `raster` 0) -> FAIL.

**Depends on `0em`** for the document population.

## Test Plan
- Unit: a hex-glyph content stream yields no words, proving the regex path is
  rejected.
- Unit: the `47` reclassification is reproduced and REFUTED - assert that
  `6. 7-Figure VSL Script Template` is present in the target list and that
  `parts == total`, so a silent `continue` cannot drop it again.
- Unit: assert `Y_TOL` digest equality at 0.0 / 0.6 / 5.0 pt on a known document.
- Unit: assert the degeneracy gate keys on `dominant_pt <= 2.0`, and that a
  7-words-per-page document with an 11.04pt dominant font is classed `text`, not
  `sparse`.
- E2E: process all 50, assert 48/2/0, assert the word total, assert zero images
  decoded.

## Considerations
- **A binary text/raster gate is WRONG here.** It was tried first and discarded:
  it classified 7 readable documents as degenerate and would have discarded real
  characters. Three classes, not two.
- **`7-Figure VSL Script Template` measured 814 words/page on one page - 80x the
  sparse threshold.** It is the least sparse document in the set. It was
  classified degenerate in the ceiling run and missed the fallback audit on a
  name mismatch, and was never separately audited. That gap is open and is
  recorded rather than smoothed over.
- The 8 documents that are neither PDF nor OOXML (6 txt, 1 png, 1 zip) are
  handled separately; the 5 `Resources Links` txt files need the §10.2 course
  prefix.
- **This gate is expected to be UNEVALUABLE until the pipeline exists.** A
  specification is not an implementation; a gate is evaluable only once code
  exists that can fail it.
- The formula lives in `stage-1/stage-1-spec.md`. If the two disagree, the SPEC
  wins and this bead is wrong - that is the correct direction of disagreement.

title: Build the test harness - real services, no mocks, detailed logging
description:
## Background
Every bead in this graph carries a Test Plan, and none of it is optional. The
gates are the deliverable's correctness argument, and a gate that has never been
run against a real artifact is a gate that might not work. **A gate that cannot
fail is not a gate** - and this project's three worst incidents (V9 matching 0
handles and passing, V8 parsing a design document instead of the deliverable, V6
passing on an empty tree) were all gates with no way to be wrong.

## Technical Approach
- **No mocks, no fakes.** A test that proves something other than what it claims
  has been the project's most frequent defect - a gate reading a design doc
  instead of the deliverable, a gate passing on an empty tree, a unit test
  asserting a match occurred rather than that the emitted value was correct.
- Real services: real ffprobe, real pypdf, real megacmd. Deepgram is exercised
  against the live API within the spend stop.
- **JSONL structured logging per test run**, with the artifact path, the input
  digest and the verdict on every line.
- Tests assert on ARTIFACTS, never on a design document.
- **Every child process gets stdin closed** - `< /dev/null` on the command line.
  `ffmpeg`, `ffprobe` and `mega-get` read stdin by default and will consume the
  loop's input stream; one handle gave two opposite verdicts across runs before
  this was found, and all pre-fix rows were discarded rather than averaged.
- **Any equality assertion needs a FLOOR: assert bytes decoded > 0 before
  asserting the hashes match.** SHA-256 of nothing equalled SHA-256 of nothing
  once, so a bit-exactness gate passed on a run that checked nothing.
- **The runner's exit code is mechanical, and the off-by-one is load-bearing:**
  ```
  exit((gate_index + 1) * 10)
  ```
  **NOT `exit(gate_index * 10)`** - that form returns **0 for V0, and 0 is
  success**, so **V0 can never report failure.** V0 is *worklist integrity:
  344 rows, never a glob*, the gate that stops a re-billed corpus. Five exit
  codes were declared for fourteen gates, and a code an implementer must map by
  hand is a code they will get wrong.

  | code | meaning |
  |---|---|
  | 0 | all gates passed |
  | 10 x N | gate N failed (N = 0, 1, 2, ...) |
  | **1** | **crash** - an exception escaped a gate, not a verdict |
  | 2 | usage error, before any gate ran |

  Exit 1 is not "a gate failed", it is "no gate reached a verdict", and a wrapper
  that treats it as a gate failure will misreport a bug as a measurement. Any gate
  failure **writes its receipt and increments its count**.

## Success Criteria
- Every gate bead's Test Plan runs green against real artifacts.
- Every gate has at least one test that PROVES IT CAN FAIL.
- Structured logs emitted for every test, with input digests.
- The runner exits `10 x (N+1)` for gate N, `1` for a crash and `2` for a usage
  error - and a deliberately thrown exception inside V0 exits 1, not 0 and not 10.

## Acceptance Criteria
**Reject a harness unless it fails on these inputs.** Three gates with no way to be
wrong caused this project's three worst incidents, and a harness that cannot
reproduce a failure is part of the defect, not a check on it.

- **A gate whose subject file is deleted** -> the runner must report that gate as
  FAILED with its receipt written and its count incremented. A harness that
  reports a green run over a missing artifact is rejected.
- **A test reading `stage-1/*.md` as its subject** -> the meta-test must catch it.
  V8 parsed a design document instead of the deliverable and passed.
- **An empty tree** passed to a gate whose only checks are ceilings -> must FAIL.
  V6 passed on an empty tree.
- **A thrown exception inside V0** -> exit **1**, not 0 and not 10. Exit 1 is not
  "a gate failed", it is "no gate reached a verdict", and a wrapper treating it as
  a gate failure misreports a bug as a measurement.
- **`exit(gate_index * 10)`** -> reject. That form returns **0 for V0, and 0 is
  success**, so V0 can never report failure. The runner must exit
  `(gate_index + 1) * 10`.
- **A killed run** -> the JSONL log carries a verdict line rather than ending
  without one.
- **Two planted defects** -> both receipts are written. A runner that stops at the
  first failure records one verdict and hides the other.
- **An equality assertion with no floor** -> reject. Plant a zero-byte decode on
  both sides: SHA-256 of nothing equalled SHA-256 of nothing once, so the
  bit-exactness gate passed on a run that checked nothing. Assert
  bytes decoded > 0 before asserting the hashes match.
- **A child process spawned without stdin closed** -> reject. One handle gave two
  opposite verdicts across runs before this was found, and all pre-fix rows were
  discarded rather than averaged.
- **`Select-Object -First N` on an upstream pipeline** -> reject. The process
  writing the output gets killed mid-run and the file looks complete.

**Recorded, not worked around:** V2 and V1's kill branch are expected to have no
failing test on this corpus - V2 is vacuous by construction (the largest part is
385 MiB against a 2 GB cap) and V1's `else` arm is unreachable (all 335 declared
sizes are KiB-exact). That is a property of the corpus, and the harness must
report those two as **unevaluable**, not as passing.

## Test Plan
- Meta: for each gate, deliberately corrupt one input and assert the gate FAILS.
  **A gate with no failing test is not a gate.**
- Meta: assert no test reads `stage-1/*.md` as its subject.
- Meta: assert the exit-code mapping for all fourteen gates, including that V0's
  failure is non-zero.
- Meta: kill a test mid-run and assert the JSONL log carries a verdict line rather
  than ending without one.

## Considerations
- V2 and V1's kill branch are **expected to have no failing test on this corpus**
  because neither can fail here - V2 is vacuous by construction (the largest part
  is 385 MiB against a 2 GB cap) and V1's `else` arm is unreachable (all 335
  declared sizes are KiB-exact). That is recorded, not worked around.
- **`Select-Object -First N` kills an upstream PowerShell pipeline** and so does
  any early-exit consumer. Capture to a variable, then slice - the process writing
  the output gets killed mid-run and the file looks complete. The same trap
  applies to a test runner that stops at the first failure: record all verdicts.
- A verdict function that can only return PASS is not a verdict. Ask *is this the
  failure mode I was testing for?*
- **This gate is expected to be UNEVALUABLE until the pipeline exists.** A
  specification is not an implementation; a gate is evaluable only once code
  exists that can fail it.
- The formula lives in `stage-1/stage-1-spec.md`. If the two disagree, the SPEC
  wins and this bead is wrong - that is the correct direction of disagreement.

title: Build 00 Topics.md - 235 rows, chronological with a topic column
description:
## Background
`00 Topics.md` answers *"where did we discuss X"*. It was thrown away during
extraction and is in scope to rebuild. It is the ONE index note the spec
mandates; `00 Home.md` is in the spec's tree as well.

**It is not a clustered index, because there are no clusters.** Measured over all
235 manifest topics: **225 groups, 221 of them singletons, largest group 3, and
only 4 of 235 units share a stem with at least one other.** The stronger
objection to rev 0's design still stands - the vault is organised by *when a call
happened*, the one axis a paying member never uses, and the topic axis was
already in every filename and required zero inference to recover. The choice was
right; the claim that it clusters was not.

**The population is 235 notes: 193 calls + 42 lessons.** 225 is a GROUP count and
344 is a TARGET count; neither is a note count and the two cannot both be true.

## Technical Approach
- Built from the emitted notes' own frontmatter, not from a separate index pass.
  **235 rows, one per emitted note, plus a `recurs` column**, each carrying ISO
  date, type, duration and a wikilink. ~250-400 lines. Linked from `00 Home.md`.
- Stems are produced by the six ordered deterministic rules in the V13 bead -
  split on the dash separator FIRST, drop qualifier segments, take the last
  surviving segment, strip the head boilerplate, keep `[a-z0-9 &+]`, fall back to
  `untitled`. **The order is load-bearing**: stripping `call` before the
  dash-split collapses 126 units to `untitled`.
- **Two distinct questions, deliberately not conflated:** this answers a jumpable
  outline ("where did we discuss X"); the per-30-minute `### 0:00` / `### 0:30`
  transcript headings answer a locate-in-call index ("where in the call is the bit
  about X"). Section 10.3 carries the second, and the headings ride on the note.
- **Cost $0.00, ~2 hours**, computed from `clean-names.json` and
  `scope-final.json`, both already on disk. No network, no STT, no vendor, no new
  dependency.

## Success Criteria
- `00 Topics.md` exists at vault root and links only to notes that exist.
- **235 rows, one per emitted note (193 calls + 42 lessons)**, not 344 and not
  225.
- Every stem is derived by the documented rules; none is authored.
- Linked from `00 Home.md`.

## Acceptance Criteria
**Reject an index unless it fails on these inputs.** The premise that topics
cluster is FALSE and measured, so these tests are about the population and the rule
order, both of which are load-bearing.

- A topic referencing a **non-existent note** -> FAIL. Every wikilink resolves.
- **225 rows or 344 rows** -> reject. 225 is a GROUP count and 344 is a TARGET
  count; the population is **235 audio units** - 193 calls + 42 lessons - the same
  population as `AUDIT.md` and as `mp4`.
- **Invert the rule order** (strip the call-type words BEFORE the dash-split) and
  assert the documented **126-unit `untitled` collapse** is reproduced. If it is
  not, the implemented order is not the documented order and the index is built on
  a different normaliser.
- `nhb coaching call - offer fundamentals - with kevin sheerin` -> takes the
  `offer fundamentals` segment, not the `kevin sheerin` segment. Skip step 3 (drop
  qualifier segments) and the corpus's most common shape becomes a person's name.
- An `untitled` stem not produced by the documented fallback -> FAIL, and every
  fallback is counted.
- A per-course, per-year or per-month **MOC tree** shipped as in scope -> reject.
  The 344 content notes are the deliverable and `00 Topics.md` is the only index
  note in scope; MOCs are optional enrichment, not counted.
- An index built from a **separate index pass** rather than the emitted notes' own
  frontmatter -> reject. It must be computed from `clean-names.json` and
  `scope-final.json`, both already on disk.

**Dependencies.** `00 Topics.md` is built from the emitted notes, so it is
downstream of `a7z`.

## Test Plan
- Unit: a topic referencing a non-existent note is caught.
- Unit: build from the emitted notes and assert exactly 235 rows, and that every
  wikilink resolves.
- Unit: the 126-unit `untitled` collapse is reproduced when the rule order is
  inverted, proving the order is load-bearing.
- E2E: the real build, 235 rows, every wikilink resolving.

## Considerations
- **A per-course, per-year and per-month index tree is NOT in scope.** The 344
  content notes are the deliverable and `00 Topics.md` is the only index note in
  scope. Shipping MOCs is optional enrichment and V6's floor is `>= 344` either
  way; they are not counted.
- It answers *"where did we discuss X"* for the 4 stems that recur and lists the
  rest once. It does not make the vault searchable in a way a full-text index
  would - that is a reader's tool, not a deliverable.
- **This gate is expected to be UNEVALUABLE until the pipeline exists.** A
  specification is not an implementation; a gate is evaluable only once code
  exists that can fail it.
- The formula lives in `stage-1/stage-1-spec.md`. If the two disagree, the SPEC
  wins and this bead is wrong - that is the correct direction of disagreement.

title: Detect channel topology per file - five branches, never corpus-wide
description:
## Background
Deepgram bills stereo at **x2**. But the corpus is MIXED: of 65 units measured in
`nhbplus-w0-channelshare-v3-2026-10-15.json`, **50 are mono, 13 are bit-identical
dual-mono, and 2 are genuinely INDEPENDENT** - `ljF0mZ4Y` (*Diving Into Data
Part 3*, mp3) and `IqVSkD5Z` (*Coffee Room Impromptu Call*, mp4). Genuinely-stereo
share is **2 of 65 = 3.08%**, 95% interval 1.0-8.5%, over 65 of 191 dated calls.
**A corpus-wide choice is wrong for at least one file in every category.**
Unconditional `-ac 1` would destroy channel separation on a per-participant file;
unconditional stereo pays 2x on files that gain nothing.

## Technical Approach
Read the channel count on the **REMUXED part, before any submission.** Its output
is the `INPUT_CHANNEL_COUNT` that `SETTLE_FROM` bills on:

```bash
ffprobe -v error -select_streams a:0 -show_entries stream=channels \
        -of default=nw=1:nk=1 "<part>.mka"
# -> 1  or  2.  Any other value is a HARD STOP, not a default.
```

`-select_streams a:0` matters: a file can carry more than one audio stream and
the first is the one submitted. `-of default=nw=1:nk=1` prints the bare number
with no key, so it is captured directly into the receipt rather than parsed.

```
channels == 1  ->  MONO.  No test, no second pass, commit once.
                   82.1% of sampled minutes are mono, and `c1` does not exist on
                   a mono input, so pan=mono|c0=c1 would ERROR on the majority
                   of parts. GUARD BEFORE MEASURING.

                   [F-MEASURE] THE pan FILTERS BELOW ARE THE BUG, REPRODUCED.
                   Running pan=mono|c0=c0 BEFORE astats collapses the stream to
                   mono, so "RMS difference dB" has no second channel left to
                   differ from and reports 0.0 - which reads as INDEPENDENT on a
                   file whose L and R are bit-identical. pjFQiLQQ showed
                   L = R = -28.585805 dB and the parse returned
                   INDEPENDENT_KEEP_STEREO_2x. The correct classifier is:

  -t 90 -i part -af astats                        (read RMS difference dB)
  -t 90 -i part -af "pan=mono|c0=c0-c1,astats"    (read RMS level of L-R)

rms_L  = ffmpeg -t 90 -i part -af astats                      -f null -
rms_R  = ffmpeg -t 90 -i part -af "pan=mono|c0=c1,astats"     -f null -
rms_D  = ffmpeg -t 90 -i part -af "pan=mono|c0=c0-c1,astats"  -f null -
delta  = rms_D - rms_L        (dB)
```

**Branch on whether L-R carries ANY signal at all**, which does not depend on dB
rounding the way a difference-in-dB comparison does.

| branch | condition | action |
|---|---|---|
| `MONO` | channels == 1 | submit as-is, settle 1x, one commit and no measurement |
| `BIT_IDENTICAL` | `delta <= -60` | `-map_channel 0.0 -c:a copy`. LOSSLESS, keeps §7.1's bit-exactness claim. Saves money. |
| `EFFECTIVELY_DUAL_MONO` | `-60 < delta <= -40` | `-ac 1` **RE-ENCODES** (a copy codec cannot change channel count). §7.1's bit-exactness claim is WITHDRAWN for these parts. Encoder and bitrate MUST be named: `-c:a libopus -b:a 32k, mono 16k`. |
| `INDEPENDENT` | `delta >= -20` | KEEP STEREO. Per-participant audio; downmixing would force acoustic diarization instead of channel-derived attribution. **Pay the 2x.** |
| `AMBIGUOUS` | otherwise | keep stereo, flag `AMBIGUOUS_CHANNELS` for the operator. **NEVER silently decide.** |

**The measurement is a 90-SECOND WINDOW, not a full decode.** Measured: `astats`
over the complete 275.93-min unit took 4m28s at 111% CPU on one core = **61.8x
realtime**, so a full-decode classifier is 9.80 core-hours = 4.90 wall-hours on
this 2-vCPU VM = **$0.56 of Azure for the measurement alone**, against 4.6 minutes
for a 90 s window over every unit. The window classifies the L/R relationship
because dual-mono is dual-mono from the first minute; the full decode buys
nothing. `channels` goes in the receipt, and the downmix decision is recorded
beside it, so the money path and the fidelity path are auditable together.

**A stereo part is up to FOUR passes, not one**: three `astats` measurements
(rms_L, rms_R and the difference signal) plus the downmix. A mono part is one
commit and no measurement.

## Success Criteria
- Every part has exactly one of the five branch labels, recorded with the part.
- `AMBIGUOUS` is never resolved by a default. It is reported.
- 2-channel `INPUT_CHANNEL_COUNT` reaches the ledger unchanged on INDEPENDENT.
- The `EFFECTIVELY_DUAL_MONO` branch exists and names its encoder and bitrate.
- The channel measurement runs inside a 90 s window, never a full decode.

## Acceptance Criteria
**Reject a classifier unless it fails on these inputs.** The `pan`-before-`astats`
bug reads as INDEPENDENT on a file whose L and R are bit-identical, so a
classifier that has not reproduced it is not known to be the fixed one.

- **Reproduce the bug:** run `pan=mono|c0=c0` BEFORE `astats` and assert it
  returns **0.0** dB. If the implementation cannot produce that, it is not running
  the corrected classifier and the branch table above it is unverified.
- `ljF0mZ4Y` and `IqVSkD5Z` -> **INDEPENDENT**, and `-ac 1 != L` on both. These
  are the only 2 of 65 measured units that are genuinely stereo. A classifier that
  returns BIT_IDENTICAL for either is a REAL DOWNMIX dressed as a lossless
  collapse, and it both destroys per-participant attribution and under-settles by
  2x.
- A `wiUyTRZb`-class part -> **BIT_IDENTICAL**, and `-map_channel` output hashes
  to channel L. `nhbplus-w0-aclose-2026-10-15.json` proved it on a 600 s window:
  L, R and `-ac 1` all hash to
  `58c695abde872bfc2da405eefb95edf300d684e9e616f6affae04dc57bc6b3d4`.
- A part in the **-40 < delta < -20** dead band -> **AMBIGUOUS**, with
  `AMBIGUOUS_CHANNELS` flagged for the operator. `AMBIGUOUS` has never fired on a
  measured input and is the one branch with no sample behind it; that is a reason
  to keep it, not to let a default decide.
- A **mono** part -> **ZERO `astats` passes** and one commit. `c1` does not exist
  on a mono input, so `pan=mono|c0=c1` would ERROR on the majority of parts - 82.1%
  of sampled minutes. Guard before measuring.
- Reject a classifier that runs a **full decode**. `astats` over the complete
  275.93-min unit took 4m28s at 111% CPU on one core = 61.8x realtime, so a
  full-decode classifier is 9.80 core-hours = 4.90 wall-hours = **$0.56 of Azure
  for the measurement alone**, against 4.6 minutes for a 90 s window over every
  unit.
- Reject any `ffmpeg` invocation with `-v error` around `astats`. It writes at
  `info` level, so every reading silently returns `-inf` - indistinguishable from
  a silent input. That trap was reproduced in the take-3 run.

**Depends on `7k7`**, because the channel count is read on the REMUXED part, before
any submission.

## Test Plan
- Unit: the two known genuinely-stereo files (`ljF0mZ4Y`, `IqVSkD5Z`) take
  INDEPENDENT. Both were independently re-verified by a second fetch and hashed on
  a 120 s window AND the full file with SHA-256, and on both `-ac 1 != L`, so
  `-ac 1` is a REAL DOWNMIX there and not a lossless collapse.
- Unit: the 13 bit-identical files take BIT_IDENTICAL and `-map_channel` output
  is hash-equal to channel L. `nhbplus-w0-aclose-2026-10-15.json` proved it on
  `wiUyTRZb.mka`, 600 s window: L, R and `-ac 1` downmix all hash to
  `58c695abde872bfc2da405eefb95edf300d684e9e616f6affae04dc57bc6b3d4`.
- Unit: the `pan=mono|c0=c0`-before-`astats` bug is reproduced and shown to
  return `0.0` dB, proving the fixed classifier is the one in use.
- Unit: a mono part performs zero `astats` passes and one commit.
- E2E: run the probe across all 235 parts, assert the branch distribution is
  recorded and no file is unlabelled.

## Considerations
- **`AMBIGUOUS` has never fired and is the one branch with no measured input.**
  It is specified, not validated. Do not delete it because a sample has not
  triggered it - that is exactly how a 2x-billing safety branch gets removed.
- **The 65-unit sample is not a gap in the population.** Channel count is read on
  every file as part of a step the pipeline performs anyway, so by the time money
  is at risk the population is exactly measured, not sampled. The sample prices the
  budget and validates the ceiling; the run replaces it with a measurement.
- **Do not invoke ffmpeg with `-v error` around `astats`.** It writes at `info`
  level, so every reading silently returns `-inf` - indistinguishable from a
  silent input. That trap was reproduced in the take-3 run.
- The stereo planning share is 3.08% (95% interval 1.0-8.5%), point estimate
  **$5.94** of extra billing. **$34.55 and $26.98 are both withdrawn** - the former
  applied the 17.9% share that v3 itself retracts as a sampling artefact, the
  latter came with the retracted measurement. Ceilings to hold against:
  **$193.04** if every dated call keeps 2 channels, **$201.83** across all 235
  units. **Not the $197.68 worst case** - the gate must STOP, not re-derive, when
  it hits a ceiling.
- **This gate is expected to be UNEVALUABLE until the pipeline exists.** A
  specification is not an implementation; a gate is evaluable only once code
  exists that can fail it.
- The formula lives in `stage-1/stage-1-spec.md`. If the two disagree, the SPEC
  wins and this bead is wrong - that is the correct direction of disagreement.

title: V2 no part reaches CAP_BYTES
description:
## Background
`CAP_BYTES = 2,000,000,000`. The largest declared part in the corpus is
**385 MiB** - 19% of the cap - so this gate **cannot fail on the corpus as it
stands**. The spec says so in its own words: *"V2 therefore passes trivially on
the corpus as it stands and CANNOT FAIL unless a future fetch exceeds 2 GB. It is
a guard against a surprise, not a check on current work."*

**`SEGMENT_SEC = 1500` is therefore also unreachable.** It is the only defence if a
future fetch exceeds the sync ceiling, and it must be re-validated against a real
part before it is relied on.

## Technical Approach
```
V2(parts) :=
    FAIL if any(p.bytes >= CAP_BYTES for p in parts)
    PASS otherwise

    NON_VACUOUS iff any(p.bytes >= 0.5 * CAP_BYTES for p in parts)
```

## Success Criteria
- V2 PASSES.
- **The non-vacuity clause is the real output.** If it is false, V2's PASS is
  vacuous and must be reported as such rather than as a meaningful pass.

## Acceptance Criteria
**This bead has no failure mode on this corpus, and that is stated rather than
worked around.** An `## Acceptance Criteria` for V2 itself would have to be
invented, and inventing one is the defect this section exists to prevent. The
honest statement is below, followed by the two things that CAN be falsified.

- Reject an implementation that prints "V2 PASS" over the real parts set. The
  required output is **"V2 PASSES, NON_VACUOUS false"** - the PASS is vacuous and
  must be labelled so, because reporting it as a meaningful pass repeats the V9
  failure in a different costume.
- **Synthetic input only:** a part of 2,000,000,001 bytes -> FAIL. That proves the
  comparator is `>=` and not `>`, and proves nothing about the corpus.
- Reject any claim that `SEGMENT_SEC = 1500` has been validated against a real
  part. It has not been reached, so it has not been validated.
- **Reject a lowered cap.** If someone moves `CAP_BYTES` to make the gate able to
  fire, the threshold was chosen backwards and the run is now segmenting parts
  that do not need it. The cap is 2,000,000,000 B.
- Reject an implementation whose segmentation branch (`7k7`) reports green on a
  corpus where it never executed. A green branch that never ran is a coverage
  claim, not a result.

## Test Plan
- Unit: a synthetic part of 2,000,000,001 bytes -> V2 FAILs.
- Unit: the real parts set -> V2 PASSes with `NON_VACUOUS` false, and that is
  recorded rather than hidden.

## Considerations
- **This gate is vacuous by construction and that is a property of the corpus,
  not a defect in the gate.** Reporting it as a meaningful pass would repeat the
  V9 failure in a different costume.
- `SEGMENT_SEC = 1500` is therefore also unreachable. It is the only defence if
  a future fetch exceeds the sync ceiling, and it must be re-validated against
  a real part before it is relied on.
- **This gate is expected to be UNEVALUABLE until the pipeline exists.** A
  specification is not an implementation; a gate is evaluable only once code
  exists that can fail it.
- The formula lives in `stage-1/stage-1-spec.md`. If the two disagree, the SPEC
  wins and this bead is wrong - that is the correct direction of disagreement.
- **Depends on `7k7`**, which produces the parts V2 measures and owns the
  `SEGMENT_SEC` branch V2 cannot reach.

title: Implement the per-PART state machine - the unit of atomicity
description:
## Background
The part, not the unit, is the unit of atomicity. A unit may be many parts; a part
is one submission attempt. Getting this wrong double-bills or loses money, and
the loss is invisible after the fact. **`reserved` means spend committed and
nothing has been sent. `sent` means the socket opened. These are different facts
and the plan must record which one happened before the crash can erase it.**

## Technical Approach
### The on-disk layout (§5.1)

`units/<UNIT_ID>/` - `state.json`, `receipt.json`, `part-NN.bin`,
`response-part-NN.json`, `assembled.json`. Atomic write+rename throughout.

### States, per spec section 5.2

```
queued -> reserved -> sent -> settled | lost
```

| state | meaning | written when | resume | never |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `queued` | Admitted to the run and **not yet committed**. No spend, no socket, no file. It is the only state that exists purely because the run is ordered. | At admission, in the same atomic write that records the reservation attempt. | **`queued` is safe to replay.** It carries no commit and nothing billed, so re-admitting every `queued` part on restart is correct and idempotent. | A `queued` part is never settled, never counted in `committed`, and never reported as `PAID_UNKNOWN`. |
| `reserved` | spend committed, nothing sent | same atomic write | release the commit, re-reserve, submit. No spend incurred. | — |
| `sent` | the socket opened - written BEFORE the request bytes leave | before the socket opens | see the recovery table | — |
| `settled` | `http_status == 200` AND `response_complete` | both recorded | skip | — |
| `lost` | the vendor gave up after accepting the bytes | the only genuinely-paid non-200 | skip | — |

**`queued` appeared in this diagram and was defined nowhere** - a state with no
meaning in a ledger that is resumed after a crash is how a part gets processed
twice. It is defined above.

**Unit completion.** A unit is complete when **every part it owns is in `settled`
or `lost`, AND the unit's assembled note exists on disk.** A unit with any part
still `queued`/`reserved`/`sent` is **not complete** and its note is not emitted.
**Partial transcripts are never published as notes** - the same principle that
makes a 504 body not a transcript, applied one level up.

### The four steps that make a write actually atomic

**"ATOMIC" WAS ASSERTED THREE TIMES AND SPECIFIED NOWHERE.** The word appears in
"Atomic write+rename throughout", in "a *single* receipt write", and in the
three-durable-bits table. None named a syscall. The recovery table's central
claim - *a kill after `sent` leaves `sent`* - rests on a durability step nobody
wrote. The four steps, named:

1. write the temp file at `<path>.tmp` in the **same directory** as the target
   (a cross-directory `rename` is not atomic on NTFS and is a copy on some mounts)
2. `f.flush()`, then `os.fsync(fd)` - flush pushes to the OS, **fsync pushes to
   the device**. Without fsync a power loss loses the bytes and `sent` is a lie.
3. `os.replace(tmp, path)` - atomic on POSIX **and** on NTFS via `MoveFileEx` with
   `REPLACE_EXISTING`. It is NOT atomic on SMB or a 9p share, which is a further
   reason the receipt ledger lives on the VM's ext4 and not on the shared mount.
4. `fsync` the **containing directory**, so the rename itself is durable. This is
   the step everyone skips, and without it the new name can be lost after a crash
   even though the bytes survive.

**The receipt is the unit of durability, and it is one file.** `status`,
`http_status`, the per-account committed amount, the part hash, the request
placeholder and the `INPUT_CHANNEL_COUNT` land in **one** `os.replace` - never
two, never a batch. A receipt half-written is worse than one not written, because
it is indistinguishable from one that was written before the socket opened.

`response_complete` exists because the response streams to disk, so **a partial
file is the normal mid-run state**: without it, `sent` + partial is
indistinguishable from `sent` + still in flight, which is the exact ambiguity this
table was written to eliminate.

### The recovery table

| On disk | Meaning | Action |
|---|---|---|
| no part file | nothing happened | redo. No spend incurred. |
| `reserved` | committed, **never sent** | release the commit, re-reserve, submit. No spend incurred. |
| `sent`, no file, `http_status` unset | in flight when the process died | `PAID_UNKNOWN`. **Never auto-resubmit. Operator decides.** |
| `sent`, **partial** file | response truncated | `PAID_UNKNOWN`. The prefix is not a transcript. Operator decides. |
| `sent`, `http_status` **402** | **credit exhausted. NOT BILLED.** | **Re-route the WHOLE PART to the secondary** per §2.2. Do **not** touch `lost`. `committed` is released, re-committed against the secondary's ledger, resubmitted. |
| `sent`, `http_status` **429** | **rate limited. NOT BILLED, and retryable.** | **Retry with exponential backoff, base 2 s, cap 60 s.** Not terminal. Not `lost`. |
| `sent`, `http_status` **400** | **malformed request. NOT BILLED.** | Re-prepare from the receipt and resubmit. Not terminal, not `lost`. |
| `sent`, `http_status` **504 / timeout / truncated** | vendor gave up **after** accepting the bytes | `PAID_UNKNOWN`, then settled as `lost`. **This is the only genuinely-paid non-200.** |

## Success Criteria
- Every state transition is persisted BEFORE the event that causes it. `sent` is
  written before the socket opens.
- A part in `PAID_UNKNOWN` is never re-submitted by any code path.
- A `queued` part never contributes to spend, in any total.
- A unit with any part outside `settled`/`lost` emits no note.
- A 429 retries with exponential backoff and is never recorded as `lost`.
- A 402 routes to the secondary and leaves `lost` untouched.

## Acceptance Criteria
**Reject a state machine unless it fails on these inputs.** "ATOMIC" was asserted
three times and specified nowhere, so these are the tests that turn the word into a
syscall sequence.

- **Kill the process between the `sent` write and the socket open.** On restart
  the part must read `PAID_UNKNOWN`, never `queued`. If it reads `queued`, the
  durability steps are asserted rather than implemented and the money moved with
  nothing on disk to prove it.
- **Interrupt a receipt write mid-way** and assert the file is either the old one
  or the new one, never a mixture. A receipt half-written is worse than one not
  written, because it is indistinguishable from one that was written before the
  socket opened.
- **Delete `response_complete`** from the schema and assert the machine fails.
  Without it, `sent` + partial is indistinguishable from `sent` + still in flight,
  which is the exact ambiguity this table was written to eliminate.
- Simulate a **429** -> retry with exponential backoff base 2 s capped at 60 s,
  and the receipt is **not** `lost`. A 429 is the single most likely transient on
  a 25-way run, and there was previously no 429 path anywhere in the document.
- Simulate a **402** -> the WHOLE PART routes to the secondary, `committed` is
  released and re-committed against the secondary's ledger, and `lost` is
  untouched. Splitting one part across accounts is a rejection.
- Simulate a **400** -> re-prepare from the receipt and resubmit. Not terminal,
  not `lost`.
- Simulate a **504 / timeout / truncated** response -> `PAID_UNKNOWN`, then
  settled as `lost`. This is the only genuinely-paid non-200.
- A unit whose parts are `settled`, `settled`, `queued` -> **emits no note.**
  Partial transcripts are never published as notes.
- Reject a machine where `queued` is undefined or un-replayable. Re-admitting
  every `queued` part on restart must be idempotent, carry no commit, and never
  contribute to `committed` or be reported as `PAID_UNKNOWN`.

## Test Plan
- Unit: the full transition table above, every row, both directions.
- Unit: kill the process between `sent` write and socket open; on restart the
  part reads `PAID_UNKNOWN`, never `queued`.
- Unit: simulate a 429 and assert the retry backoff doubles to a 60 s cap and the
  receipt is not `lost`.
- Unit: simulate a 400 and assert re-prepare + resubmit, not `lost`.
- Unit: a receipt write interrupted mid-way leaves either the old file or the new
  one, never a mixture.
- E2E: a simulated 402 stops the run and leaves committed spend intact.

## Considerations
- **`lost` was a wrong RULE, not a wrong number.** `lost iff (http_status != 200)`
  made R4 re-measure across every declared size, because it charges the vendor
  for a timeout it had already given up on and makes a 429 terminal - and a 429
  is the single most likely transient on a 25-way run. There was previously **no
  429 path anywhere in this document.**
- Write-ahead ordering is the entire protection. If `sent` is not durable before
  the socket opens, a crash in between loses the only evidence the money moved.
- **This gate is expected to be UNEVALUABLE until the pipeline exists.** A
  specification is not an implementation; a gate is evaluable only once code
  exists that can fail it.
- The formula lives in `stage-1/stage-1-spec.md`. If the two disagree, the SPEC
  wins and this bead is wrong - that is the correct direction of disagreement.
close_reason: Built pipeline/scripts/part-state.py (queued/reserved/sent/settled/lost, atomic 4-step write, 402/429/400/504 table, PAID_UNKNOWN never resubmitted) + test-part-state.py; 11/11 pass, log pipeline/out/part-state-tests.jsonl

title: Implement the single global spend ledger
description:
## Background
One ledger, one writer. Two ledgers means two truths and a reconciliation that
never reconciles. Rev 0 said "reserved under `flock`" with **no file and no
path**, while every named artifact was per-**unit** - and a per-unit lock cannot
serialise a global sum: 16 workers can each read a stale total and jointly
overshoot.

`SPEND_HARD_STOP_USD` is **$213.48** and is DERIVED, one formula and one figure:

    (34,472.10 calls + 294.84 undated tail + 1,569.62 lessons) x $0.0056
      = $203.48
    + $10.00 loss reserve
      = $213.48

That constant carried **four different values at once** - $207.31 (the budget
artifact), $207.35 (the spec, twice), $207.68 (labelled "DERIVED, not asserted")
and $203.48 - and the block that insisted it was derived was itself the wrong
one. It is now computed from the formula above, and `pipeline/out/PLAN-TRUTH.json`
carries `STOP: 213.48` for the same reason. **Quote ONE value: $213.48.**

Credit position: **no payment card on file**, so the vendor itself enforces a
backstop - exhausting the credit returns **HTTP 402** and processing stops. But
$200 < $213.48, so the 402 fires at **$200 per account**, strictly BELOW our own
gate. Two accounts are therefore required:

```
primary    DEEPGRAM_API_KEY     carries the bulk
secondary  DEEPGRAM_API_KEY_2   carries the shortfall above one account's $200
```

The secondary is a **wallet, not a worker**. Deepgram scopes concurrency per
project, so a second key adds zero throughput, and distributing traffic
concurrently across accounts is a documented ToS violation.

## Technical Approach
### Schema and lock (§5.3)

```
LEDGER = /data/nhb/_meta/spend.json     PER ACCOUNT:
    {"accounts": {
        "<account_id>": {"committed":USD,"settled":USD,"lost":USD,"released":USD}},
     "totals":      {"committed":USD,"settled":USD,"lost":USD,
                     "released":USD}}
LOCK   = /data/nhb/_meta/spend.lock     flock, held across READ-CHECK-WRITE
```

The `released` field was OMITTED while every per-account object declared it, so the
gate formula was stated over a field the schema did not have. It is present in
both places. The ledger is **per-account**, not a single global object - an
implementer following a global-pool description would build one pool and the
second key would never be used.

Commit and settle are each one atomic ledger mutation under that one lock:

```
commit:   committed += cost
settle:   committed -= cost;  settled += actual
release:  committed -= cost;  released += cost
lost:     committed -= cost;  lost    += actual
```

**`release` is compare-and-set INSIDE the flock**: read `released`; if this
`part_id` is not already in the released set, add the cost and add `part_id`.
Two resume passes over one part would otherwise double-count, and a
double-counted release frees budget that was never spent - **which is how a hard
stop becomes a soft one without any code appearing to change.** **A `reserved`
part is released ONCE.**

### The two quantities, defined once

```
COMMIT_COST = (billed_seconds(part) / 60) * (RATE + KEYTERM_RATE)

              RATE_USD_PER_MIN        = 0.0043   nova-3 monolingual, PRE-RECORDED,
                                               Pay As You Go. Sourced and dated.
                                               Diarization INCLUDED on
                                               pre-recorded, so diarize=true
                                               costs $0.00.
              KEYTERM_RATE_USD/MIN    = 0.0013   ADOPTED, operator decision
                                               2026-10-15, A/B-measured.
              PER_REQUEST_MINIMUM    = NONE      True per-second billing, no
                                               minimum, no rounding. The
                                               pessimistic ceil was deleted.

SETTLE_FROM  = metadata.duration seconds x INPUT_CHANNEL_COUNT,
              IDENTICALLY in the 7.2 gate and in V10.
```

**The `/60` is not cosmetic.** `RATE` and `KEYTERM_RATE` are USD PER MINUTE while
`billed_seconds` is SECONDS. Without the division a 3,600 s part commits $20.16
instead of $0.336 and the corpus commits $11,764.40 instead of $196.07 - a **60x
OVERCOMMIT** that would stop the run after roughly ten parts. This is the same
unit slip that produced the 273.7x error, and it is closed by this fix.

`SETTLE_FROM` is **NOT** the response's channel array: Deepgram returns
`channels=1` for a stereo input while BILLING 2x. **NOT** the pre-downmix part:
the 7.1a BIT_IDENTICAL branch re-runs `-map_channel` and produces a MONO part, so
reading the pre-downmix count would settle every downmixed unit at 2x and
double-count the saving. `INPUT_CHANNEL_COUNT` is recorded in the SAME atomic
write as `sent`.

**Billing uses the DECODED duration, never a container header.** `pjFQiLQQ`'s
header claims 4,958.7 s while its decoded PCM is 5,431.8 s (**+9.54%**); a
header-derived reservation is under-reserved by exactly the header's error, per
part, silently. The header/decoded gap is per-file, not a corpus-wide constant -
`wiUyTRZb` agrees to 1 ms.

### Reconciliation is derived, never authoritative

`bin/rescan.py` rebuilds the ledger from `receipt.json` parts, and **receipts
win** on conflict. This keeps single-authority (no desync) while giving the
global sum a named home. SQLite, a journal and per-unit JSON are all rejected as
independent truths.

### The report — two cost lines, never one

Every report this bead emits carries **two money figures side by side, as
separate fields**: STT spend from the ledger, and **VM-days** from the compute
box. They come from different meters, they move independently, and the run's
total cost is not knowable from either alone. A report with one combined figure
is a report that cannot be checked against either vendor's invoice.

```
report := {
  "stt_forecast_usd":  float,   # from the $213.48 derivation
  "stt_actual_usd":    float,   # from the ledger, committed + lost
  "vm_days_forecast":  float,   # compute box, Azure Standard_D2s_v5
  "vm_days_actual":    float,   # uptime of the run
  ... ledger totals ...
}
```

**The VM-day VALUE is deliberately not asserted anywhere in this bead.** §15
records Azure VM-days for a 16-way run over 605.61 h as **UNMEASURED**, and
under the project's own rule an unmeasured figure is not written down as if it
were measured. What IS asserted is presence, separateness, and that a reader
cannot silently drop the line. That is a checkable property; a guessed number is
not.

## Success Criteria
- Running committed spend, read from the ledger, never exceeds **$213.48**, on
  either account individually and on the sum.
- `PAID_UNKNOWN` parts contribute their upper bound against the stop.
- The ledger is derivable to the cent from receipts alone, by `bin/rescan.py`,
  with receipts winning every conflict.
- A `reserved` part released twice does not change `released` the second time.
- Forecast and actual stay separate in every report; **VM-days are reported
  alongside STT spend as their own named fields, not folded into a single
  "total cost" number.** The presence of the VM-day line is what is asserted;
  its value is unmeasured (§15) and is not claimed here.

## Acceptance Criteria
**Reject a ledger implementation unless it fails on these inputs.** A double-counted
release frees budget that was never spent, which is how a hard stop becomes a soft
one without any code appearing to change.

- **Two resume passes over one `reserved` part** -> `released` changes once. The
  release must be compare-and-set INSIDE the flock: read `released`, add the cost
  and add `part_id` only if `part_id` is not already in the set. An implementation
  that releases unconditionally on a second pass frees money it never spent.
- A 3,600 s part -> `committed = $0.336`. A ledger reporting **$20.16** has
  dropped the `/60`; the corpus then commits **$11,764.40 instead of $196.07**, a
  60x OVERCOMMIT that stops the run after roughly ten parts. This is the same unit
  slip that produced the 273.7x error.
- A stereo part with `INPUT_CHANNEL_COUNT == 2` -> settles **2x** even though the
  response says 1 channel object. Deepgram returns `channels=1` for a stereo input
  while BILLING 2x.
- A BIT_IDENTICAL part that was downmixed -> settles **1x**. Reading the
  pre-downmix count settles every downmixed unit at 2x.
- `bin/rescan.py` over the lessons census receipts -> **$8.79** to the cent
  (1,569.6167 min x $0.0056). **The 42 bonus lesson videos were in no budget line
  for several rounds** - they are in scope, ordered, submitted and counted in the
  vault tree, and they carry 1,569.6167 MEASURED minutes. A ledger missing them is
  $8.79 short and the reserve is 87.9% consumed before the first request.
- Reject a ledger that excludes `PAID_UNKNOWN` from the running total. Unknown
  money is spent money; excluding it makes the gate pass by not knowing.
- Reject a single global pool. The ledger is **per-account**: an implementer
  following a global-pool description builds one pool, the second key is never
  used, and the $200-per-account 402 backstop is unobservable.
- Reject a ledger where `totals.released` is missing while every per-account
  object declares it. The `released` field was OMITTED from `totals` while the
  gate formula was stated over it - the schema did not have the field the formula
  needed.
- **Reject a report with no VM-day field, or with one combined "total cost"
  field.** This criterion was previously untestable: it was stated as a Success
  Criterion and appeared in no test, so it could not fail. Now it can - see the
  mutation check in the Test Plan. **Assert the two fields exist and are
  distinct, then delete the VM-day field and assert the test FAILS.** A presence
  test that cannot fail is the same defect as a gate that matches nothing.
- Reject a report where `stt_actual_usd` and `stt_forecast_usd` are the same
  variable, or where `vm_days_actual` is derived from the STT total. They are
  different meters; conflating them makes the forecast check circular.

**Dependencies.** The ledger settles from `INPUT_CHANNEL_COUNT`, which is the
channel detector's output (`geo`), and the atomic-write discipline is `kgb`'s.

## Test Plan
- Unit: a stereo part with `INPUT_CHANNEL_COUNT == 2` settles at 2x even though
  the response says 1 channel object.
- Unit: a BIT_IDENTICAL part that was downmixed settles at 1x, not 2x.
- Unit: a 3,600 s part commits $0.336, not $20.16 - the `/60` assertion, run
  explicitly.
- Unit: two resume passes over the same `reserved` part release it once.
- E2E: replay the receipts from the lessons census and assert the total equals
  **$8.79** to the cent (1,569.6167 min x $0.0056).
- Unit: render the report and assert it carries `vm_days_forecast` and
  `vm_days_actual` **beside** `stt_forecast_usd` and `stt_actual_usd`, as four
  distinct keys. This is the test the VM-day Success Criterion lacked.
- Unit (MUTATION, and this is the part that makes the criterion falsifiable):
  delete the `vm_days_actual` field from the renderer and assert the report test
  above **FAILS**. Delete it and the test still passes, and the criterion is a
  decoration again. Record the mutation in the test output.
- Unit: assert no single field equals the sum of STT and VM cost. A combined
  total defeats the point of reporting them separately.

## Considerations
- **Excluding `PAID_UNKNOWN` makes the gate pass by not knowing.** Unknown money
  is spent money. It counts against the stop at its upper bound.
- The loss reserve is **$10.00**, 5% of ~235 units at the mean COMMIT_COST $0.86
  = $9.89. It is not a contingency for a bad estimate; it is the rounding
  reserve. $10 leaves 1.1% headroom, which is marginal and is stated as marginal.
- **The 42 bonus lesson videos were in no budget line for several rounds.** They
  are in scope (§1), ordered (§9 step 3), submitted (§7.2, "every submission") and
  counted in the vault tree. They carry 1,569.6167 MEASURED min = $8.79 and
  appeared nowhere, so $213.48 was $8.79 short and the reserve was 87.9%
  consumed before the first request. **A missing number is the one class a
  propagation sweep cannot catch, because there is nothing to propagate.**
- **VM-days are asserted as PRESENT, never as a number.** §15 lists Azure VM-days
  for a 16-way run over 605.61 h among the figures that are unmeasured because
  nothing has been paid for yet. Writing a plausible figure here would repeat the
  four-values-for-one-constant failure this bead's Background records. The test
  asserts the field exists, is separate, and that removing it breaks a test.
- **This gate is expected to be UNEVALUABLE until the pipeline exists.** A
  specification is not an implementation; a gate is evaluable only once code
  exists that can fail it.
- The formula lives in `stage-1/stage-1-spec.md`. If the two disagree, the SPEC
  wins and this bead is wrong - that is the correct direction of disagreement.

title: V12 identity binding - every note resolves to its unit
description:
## Background
V12 is the most important gate in the spec, and the reason is narrow: **V7 proves
determinism, not correctness.** V7 re-runs the same renderer on the same inputs.
If assembly cross-wires two units' responses - a file-handle reuse, an off-by-one
in `part-NN` offset concatenation - V7 reproduces the mistake byte-perfectly and
reports success. No other gate binds the identity of the *content* to the
identity of the *unit it landed in*. That is what V12 is for.

Clauses 5 and 6 were mutually exclusive in an earlier revision, which had also
deleted the `request_id` column from `AUDIT.md` on the strength of
"`request_id` is None for EVERY submission". Two later artifacts contradict that:
`nhbplus-w0-asynccontract-2026-10-15.json` carries None, while
`nhbplus-w0-syncceiling3-2026-10-15.json` carries `01a13ec6-9208-7c90-a68d-0209a8e6be33`
and `deepgram-eu-limits-and-chain-proof-2026-10-15.json` carries
`01a13cfc-1b03-7e10-94cb-a448d81cb512`. Whether `request_id` is present on the sync
path generally or only on some request shapes is **still not established** - two
present, one absent, three probes. Clause 5 is worded to be falsifiable either
way; do not read that as evidence the question is settled.

## Technical Approach
```
V12(assembled, receipts, vault_dir) :=

  For each audio unit U:                                     # 235 units
   1. H(U) = SHA-256 of the ordered concatenation of every
             utterances[*].transcript in U/assembled.json
   2. H(U) equals the value recorded in U/receipt.json at
             assembly time
   3. H(U) values are PAIRWISE DISTINCT across all 235 audio units
   4. EXACTLY ONE note under vault/ renders utterance text hashing to H(U)
   5. no two units share a NON-NULL request_id
       # worded for the null case so it is falsifiable either way. The clause
       # as first written ("no request_id appears under two different unit
       # ids") FAILED on a flawless run, because None appears under all 235.
   6. effective_spend reconciles to COMMIT_COST, and ffprobe(U) is within 2% of
       the metadata.duration in U's OWN stored response
       # re-worded to bind ffprobe(U) to U's OWN response, NOT to a request_id
       # lookup, so it no longer depends on that field existing at all

  NON_VACUOUS iff len(audio_units) == 235 and every clause above was evaluated
```

**Why it cannot fail trivially.** `H` is computed from the **raw response**, not
from the rendered note, so re-running the renderer cannot satisfy it. Clause 4 is
load-bearing: if two units' transcripts were exchanged, both `H` values still
exist on disk and **V7 still passes** - but each note now renders the other's
hash, so clause 4 fails for **both** units. A single swap is caught twice.
Clauses 5 and 6 catch the same defect at the vendor and money boundaries.

**Cost $0.00** - a hash over strings already on disk, well under a second.

## Success Criteria
- All six clauses evaluated on all 235 audio units, with the count recorded.
- Clause 3 holds: 235 distinct `H` values, no collision.
- Clause 4 holds: each `H(U)` is rendered by exactly one note under `vault/`.
- `request_id` is recorded on every receipt and in `AUDIT.md` - **blank if
  absent, never invented**.
- Swapping two units' transcripts in a test tree fails V12 for BOTH units while
  V7 still passes.

## Acceptance Criteria
**Reject a V12 unless it fails on these inputs.** A manifest/receipt/ledger
traceability check is NOT V12 - it cannot detect an exchange of content between two
units, which is the one defect V12 was created for.

- **Exchange two units' `assembled.json` contents** in a two-unit test tree ->
  clause 4 fails for **BOTH** units, and V7 still passes. A single swap must be
  caught twice. A V12 that passes an exchange has been reduced to the check
  V7/V9/V10 already cover, and is rejected.
- Force an **`H` collision** between two units -> clause 3 fails.
- Duplicate one unit's `request_id` on another -> clause 5 fails.
- A receipt whose `request_id` is `null` -> clause 5 **still evaluates**: no crash,
  and no vacuous pass. `None` appears under all 235 and the original wording
  ("no request_id appears under two different unit ids") FAILED on a flawless run.
- **Break the duration binding** - hold `ffprobe(U)` against another unit's stored
  response - and assert clause 6 fails the unit whose duration moved. Clause 6
  binds `ffprobe(U)` to U's OWN response, **not** to a `request_id` lookup, so it
  no longer depends on that field existing at all.
- Omit `utterances=true` from a submission -> V12 becomes **unevaluable** and must
  be reported as such, never green. `assembled.json` is built from
  `results.utterances`; without it there is nothing to hash.
- Fewer than 235 audio units -> `NON_VACUOUS` is false and the gate must not
  report green.

**Dependencies.** V12 evaluates the assembled tree (`a7z`) and hashes the response
that `z72` retrieved.

## Test Plan
- Unit: build a two-unit tree, exchange their `assembled.json` contents, and
  assert V12 clause 4 fails for both while V7 passes. **This is the regression
  test for the defect V12 exists to catch.**
- Unit: force an `H` collision between two units -> clause 3 fails.
- Unit: duplicate one unit's `request_id` on another -> clause 5 fails.
- Unit: a receipt whose `request_id` is None -> clause 5 still evaluates (does
  not crash, does not pass vacuously).
- E2E: all 235 units bound, with the distinct-hash count printed as evidence.

## Considerations
- **`assembled.json` is built from `results.utterances`,** which is why
  `utterances=true` is non-optional on the request (§7.2.0). Without it there is
  nothing to hash and V12 is unevaluable.
- **A manifest/receipt/ledger traceability check is NOT V12.** An earlier draft of
  this bead asserted only that every note resolves to a manifest row, a settled
  receipt and a ledger entry. That check is already covered by V7, V9 and V10; it
  cannot detect an exchange of content between two units, which is the one defect
  V12 was created for. Do not substitute it for the clauses above.
- The 109 documents are not V12's subject. `AUDIT.md` is **235 lines, one per
  audio unit**, and the documents are verified by §11's path and frontmatter
  gates instead.
- **This gate is expected to be UNEVALUABLE until the pipeline exists.** A
  specification is not an implementation; a gate is evaluable only once code
  exists that can fail it.
- The formula lives in `stage-1/stage-1-spec.md`. If the two disagree, the SPEC
  wins and this bead is wrong - that is the correct direction of disagreement.

title: V6 nothing media-shaped under vault/ - and a floor
description:
## Background
Constraint 1 is absolute: nothing media-shaped touches the operator's PC. The
finished markdown vault IS the deliverable and does land there. Every check
below is a **CEILING**, and `vault/` currently holds **0 files** - an empty tree
satisfies all of them and returns PASS. That is this project's own
empty-vs-empty trap.

## Technical Approach
```
V6(vault_dir) :=
    BANNED = mp3|mp4|mp4v|mov|m4a|wav|flac|mka|aac|opus|ogg|mpga|mkv|webm
             | pdf|docx|doc|rtf|odt|pptx|ppt|xlsx|xls|csv|txt
             | png|jpg|jpeg|gif|svg|bmp|tif|tiff|webp
    FAIL if any(p.suffix.lstrip(".").lower() in BANNED for p in vault_dir.rglob("*"))
    FAIL if any(re.search(r"\.(mp3|mp4|mov|m4a|wav|flac|mka)$", p.name, re.I)
                for p in vault_dir.rglob("*"))
    FAIL if (vault_dir / "attachments").exists()      # C1: does not ship

    n = len(list(vault_dir.rglob("*.md")))
    FAIL if n < 344          # >= not ==
    NON_VACUOUS iff n >= 344
```

**`>= 344`, not `== 344`:** the spec's own tree also names `00 Home.md` and
`00 Topics.md`, so a flawless run emits 346 and an equality test would fail it.
The floor's job is to stop an empty tree reading as PASS; it is not a manifest.

## Success Criteria
- V6 FAILS on a planted `.mp4`, a planted `.docx`, and a planted `.png`.
- V6 FAILS on an empty tree.
- V6 FAILS if `attachments/` exists.
- **V6 runs on the VM source tree, BEFORE the copy to the PC.** Once a media
  file lands there, Constraint 1 has already been violated.

## Acceptance Criteria
**Every clause above the floor is a CEILING, so an empty tree satisfies all of them.
Reject a V6 unless it fails on each of these:**

- **An empty `vault/` directory** -> FAIL on the floor. This is the input that
  matters: it is the project's own empty-vs-empty trap, and V6 passed on it once.
- A 344-note tree with ONE planted `.mp4` -> FAIL. And with a `.docx`, a `.png`, an
  `.mka`, a `.txt`. Each banned extension is its own input; a V6 that catches audio
  and misses documents passes a Constraint 1 breach.
- A tree with `attachments/` present, even an EMPTY one -> FAIL. C1 says it does
  not ship, and an empty directory is still a directory.
- A tree whose only `.md` files are index notes (`00 Home.md`, `00 Topics.md`) and
  no content notes -> FAIL on the floor. A V6 that counts any `.md` passes.
- **A flawless 346-note tree** -> PASS. Reject a V6 that enforces `== 344`; the
  spec's own tree names `00 Home.md` and `00 Topics.md` too.
- **The placement test:** plant a `.mp3` in the VM source tree and run the egress
  sequence. Reject a V6 wired downstream of the copy - it must FAIL the run before
  `scp`. W0-Egress proved `scp -r` copied a planted `.mp3` faithfully, which is
  correct behaviour for a binary pipe. The control belongs upstream of the only
  irreversible step.

**Dependencies.** V6 is evaluated over the assembled tree (`a7z`) and must exist
before `dgu` may run its sequence.

## Test Plan
- Unit: each banned extension, planted, is caught.
- Unit: `attachments/` present -> FAIL.
- Unit: empty tree -> FAIL on the floor, not PASS.
- E2E: the real vault, 344+ notes, zero banned extensions.

## Considerations
- `attachments/` was mandated by `VAULT-STRUCTURE.md`, which held raw
  `docx`/`pptx`/`xlsx` "as fetched" - **the Constraint 1 violation, written
  into the deliverable's structure by a subordinate document.** It does not
  ship. That file is now explicitly subordinate to the spec.
- `.mka` is in the banned set because it is the container the remux produces. The
  gate must run where the remuxed parts are NOT.
- **This gate is expected to be UNEVALUABLE until the pipeline exists.** A
  specification is not an implementation; a gate is evaluable only once code
  exists that can fail it.
- The formula lives in `stage-1/stage-1-spec.md`. If the two disagree, the SPEC
  wins and this bead is wrong - that is the correct direction of disagreement.

title: V0 worklist integrity - 344 rows, never a glob
description:
## Background
Every gate downstream is checked against the worklist, so its construction
decides what the run believes exists. `scope-final.json` holds 344 rows:
193 calls + 42 lesson videos + 109 documents.

**Provenance of 344, and it is measured, not estimated: 193 + 42 + 109.** The 100
MP4 alternates are recorded in the manifest and **never fetched** - a route change,
not a removal (Rule 1). `scope-final.json`'s kinds are `audio` / `written_hand` /
`course_doc` / `orphan_doc` (235 / 37 / 36 / 36, measured in `by_kind`), while
`manifest-v3.json` spells the call kind **`calls`** and the lesson kind
**`lessons`** (193 / 42, 235 total, measured). **There is no kind called `call`,
singular, in either file** - and that is the spelling the old V9 matcher asked for,
which is why it hit 0 handles and passed over a dropped call. The spelling that is
correct on `manifest-v3.json` is `calls`, with an `s`; the spelling that is correct
on `scope-final.json` is `audio`. They name different populations, and V0 must not
be asked to reconcile them.

**This bead depends on `0em` (the worklist construction) and on `emn` (the test
harness).** It is the first gate to run, so nothing about it is provable until the
harness exists, and its input is the artifact `0em` emits.

## Technical Approach
```
V0(scope_final, manifest_v3, clean_names) :=
    # NEVER a glob. A glob derives its population from whatever is on disk, so a
    # fetch that silently produced nothing yields an empty worklist and every
    # downstream count agrees with it. DECLARE the population, then CHECK it.
    rows = scope_final.targets                    # 344, and they are TARGETS
    FAIL if len(rows) != 344                      # 193 calls + 42 lessons + 109 docs
    FAIL if len({r.handle for r in rows}) != 344  # handles are unique

    # TWO SEPARATE EQUALITIES, NOT ONE - a MEASURED correction.
    # The first version compared all 344 scope handles against manifest's 235 and
    # treated inequality as a failure. MEASURED 2026-10-16: scope-final holds 344
    # targets with 344 unique handles; manifest-v3 holds 235 units whose handles
    # are a SUBSET - all 235 present, 0 missing, 109 handles in scope that
    # manifest does not carry, because those 109 are the DOCUMENTS.
    # The single-equality form therefore FAILS ON EVERY CORRECT RUN.
    # It also made the old NON_VACUOUS clause UNSATISFIABLE: `344 == 235` is
    # false, so a correct run could never report non-vacuous.
    audio_rows = [r for r in rows if r.kind == "audio"]
    doc_rows   = [r for r in rows
                  if r.kind in ("written_hand", "course_doc", "orphan_doc")]

    FAIL if len(audio_rows) != 235
    FAIL if {r.handle for r in audio_rows} !=
            {u.media.handle for u in manifest_v3.units}   # exactly the 235 units
    FAIL if len(doc_rows) != 109
    FAIL if {r.handle for r in doc_rows} !=
            {d.handle for d in clean_names.documents}     # exactly the 109 docs

    non_vacuous := (len(rows) == 344
                    and len(audio_rows) == 235 == len(manifest_v3.units)
                    and len(doc_rows) == 109 == len(clean_names.documents))
```
Provenance of 344: 193 + 42 + 109, all three measured, not estimated.

## Success Criteria
- V0 PASSES on a correct run and **FAILS** on a run where one row was dropped,
  duplicated, or mis-spelled.
- The non-vacuity clause fires when the worklist is built from a directory
  listing instead of the declared file.

## Acceptance Criteria
**This bead's job is to make the run's population unreachable from the disk.** Reject
an implementation unless each of the following FAILs rather than passes:

- A `scope-final.json` copy with ONE row deleted -> V0 FAIL, and the FAIL names the
  count. A V0 that reports 344 over a 343-row input has read the wrong file.
- A copy with one row DUPLICATED -> FAIL on handle uniqueness, not on the row count.
- A worklist built from a glob of a **partial** directory -> FAIL on set inequality
  with `manifest-v3.json`. This is the input that matters most: the glob satisfies
  every count derived from the same directory.
- An **empty** `scope-final.json` -> FAIL. A V0 that returns PASS on zero rows is the
  V9 failure with a different formula, and it is the one input a worklist builder
  meets in practice when a fetch silently produces nothing.
- A tree where the on-disk enumeration and `worklist/targets.csv` disagree -> the
  verdict must follow the CSV. If it follows the disk, the population was discovered,
  not declared.
- Reject outright if any gate in the graph reads its population from a directory
  listing at verification time. `br dep list` shows `0em` and `emn` are the only
  prerequisites; V0 is the bead that makes a glob impossible downstream, and the
  test harness (`emn`) must assert the absence.

## Test Plan
- Unit: delete one row from a copy of scope-final -> V0 FAILs with the count.
- Unit: duplicate one row -> V0 FAILs on uniqueness.
- Unit: build from a glob of a partial directory -> V0 FAILs on set inequality.
- E2E: V0 PASSES against the real artifacts.

## Considerations
- **A glob derives its population from whatever is on disk.** A fetch that
  silently produced nothing yields an empty worklist and every downstream count
  agrees with it. Declare the population, then check it. Never discover it.
- `scope-final.json`'s kinds are `audio` / `written_hand` / `course_doc` /
  `orphan_doc`, measured in its `by_kind`: audio 235 / written_hand 37 /
  course_doc 36 / orphan_doc 36. `manifest-v3.json` spells the call kind `calls`
  (193) and the lesson kind `lessons` (42), 235 units in total. **No kind called
  `call`, singular, exists in either file** - which is the spelling that let V9's
  old matcher hit 0 handles and pass.
- **Provenance of 344:** `pipeline/out/PLAN-TRUTH.json` `N_TARGETS: 344`,
  `N_CALLS: 193`, `N_AUDIO: 235`; `scope-final.json` `totals` and `targets`
  (344 rows, 338 carrying a declared size); `manifest-v3.json` 235 units.
- **This gate is expected to be UNEVALUABLE until the pipeline exists.** A
  specification is not an implementation; a gate is evaluable only once code
  exists that can fail it.
- The formula lives in `stage-1/stage-1-spec.md`. If the two disagree, the SPEC
  wins and this bead is wrong - that is the correct direction of disagreement.


Dependencies:
  -> nhbplus-corpus-emn (blocks) - Build the test harness - real services, no mocks, detailed logging
  -> nhbplus-corpus-0em (blocks) - Construct the 344-row worklist from scope-final.json, never a glob

title: V4 three-way duration reconcile
description:
## Background
Three durations exist per unit and they do not agree. `pjFQiLQQ` is the corpus's
known divergence: container header **4,958.7 s** against decoded **5,431.8 s**,
**+9.54%** measured header-relative. Every other unit measured agrees to within a
millisecond (`16,556.208` vs `16,556.207`). So the rule cannot be "they must
match" - it must be "disagreement is bounded, and the larger value wins for
billing."

## Technical Approach
```
V4(d_manifest, d_header, d_decoded) :=
    d_authoritative := d_decoded        # the only MEASUREMENT of the audio
    spread := max(d_manifest, d_header, d_decoded)
              - min(d_manifest, d_header, d_decoded)
    ratio  := spread / d_authoritative

    FAIL if d_decoded is missing          # no decoded value = no authority
    FAIL if ratio > 0.10                  # DURATION_TOLERANCE
    WARN and record if ratio > 0.02       # 2%: worth a human glance
    PASS otherwise

    NON_VACUOUS iff d_decoded is not None
```

**A sentinel `d_manifest` is EXCLUDED from the spread entirely.** It is a display
value; including it manufactures disagreement that is not there. `pjFQiLQQ`
slipped through the duration check only because its recorded `dur_s` was **0** -
the exact class of unit the check exists for.

**Billing uses `d_authoritative`, not `d_manifest`.** On `pjFQiLQQ` that is the
difference between 4,958.7 and 5,431.8 s - the 286.9-minute tail that was an
estimate is now **294.84 measured**. Billing from the header would have
under-charged by 9.54% on that unit and never shown why.

**The two ratios are not the same number, and the difference is 0.8 points.**
`+9.54%` is header-relative: `(5,431.8 - 4,958.7) / 4,958.7 = 0.0954`. V4's own
`ratio` is authoritative-relative: `4,958.7... spread / d_decoded =
473.1 / 5,431.8 = **0.0871**`. Both are below the 0.10 tolerance and both are
above the 0.02 WARN band, so the verdict is unchanged - but a test asserting the
formula's output must assert **0.0871**, not 0.0954.

## Success Criteria
- All 235 units reconcile, or fail loudly.
- `pjFQiLQQ` settles on its DECODED duration, 5,431.8 s.
- The WARN band is exercised by at least one unit so the threshold is not dead.
- A unit with a sentinel or zero `d_manifest` has a spread computed from header
  and decoded only.

## Acceptance Criteria
**Reject a V4 unless it fails on these inputs.** The two ratios differ by 0.8
points and a test asserting the wrong one passes an implementation with the wrong
formula.

- `pjFQiLQQ`'s three values -> **ratio 0.0871** and WARN, not FAIL. An
  implementation reporting **0.0954** has computed the header-relative ratio; the
  formula's `spread / d_authoritative` is 473.1 / 5,431.8. Both are below the 0.10
  tolerance and both above the 0.02 WARN band, so the verdict is identical either
  way - **which is exactly why a test must assert the number, not the verdict.**
- A `d_manifest` of 2 GiB with a real decoded value -> FAIL. That FAIL is proof
  the sentinel was included in the spread, which manufactures disagreement that is
  not there. A V4 that returns PASS here has a broken exclusion.
- `d_manifest = 0` with no decoded value -> FAIL. `pjFQiLQQ` slipped through the
  duration check only because its recorded `dur_s` was 0, the exact class of unit
  the check exists for.
- A 12% divergence -> FAIL, proving the tolerance can bite.
- **A 1 ms divergence** -> PASS. `wiUyTRZb`, the corpus maximum at 275.93 min /
  16,556.207 s, has its header and decoded values agreeing to **1 ms**
  (16,556.208 vs 16,556.207) - not `pjFQiLQQ`, which is the +9.54% divergence.
  Two units, two facts; do not cite one for the other. So "they must match" is
  not the rule; disagreement is bounded and the larger value wins for billing.
  Source: `evidence/probes/nhbplus-w0-remux-2026-10-15.json` and the spec's
  §11.3 V4 preamble.
- Reject a V4 whose ledger row for `pjFQiLQQ` reads 4,958.7 s. The decoded value
  is the one that must be written; billing from the header under-charges by 9.54%
  on that unit and never shows why.

**Dependencies.** V4 runs on remuxed parts (`7k7`) and on submitted audio (`z72`),
because `d_decoded` is only available once the part exists.

## Test Plan
- Unit: `pjFQiLQQ`'s three values -> **ratio 0.0871**, WARN not FAIL.
- Unit: a sentinel `d_manifest` of 2 GiB with a real decoded value -> spread
  computed from header and decoded only, and the sentinel excluded.
- Unit: a 12% divergence -> FAIL, proving the tolerance can bite.
- E2E: all 235, assert zero FAILs and assert the decoded value is the one
  written to the ledger.

## Considerations
- **The header/decoded gap is per-file, not a corpus-wide constant.** One measured
  unit agreed to 1 ms. **Do not apply `pjFQiLQQ`'s 9.54% as a correction factor
  anywhere.**
- The manifest durations were sound on a 10-MP3 stratified sample (all within
  0.02% of decoded truth); `pjFQiLQQ` slipped through only because its `dur_s`
  was 0.
- **This gate is expected to be UNEVALUABLE until the pipeline exists.** A
  specification is not an implementation; a gate is evaluable only once code
  exists that can fail it.
- The formula lives in `stage-1/stage-1-spec.md`. If the two disagree, the SPEC
  wins and this bead is wrong - that is the correct direction of disagreement.

title: V7 reduction diff - the vault is a pure function of receipts
description:
## Background
If the vault is not derivable from the receipts, the receipts are decorative and
V10's spend arithmetic is built on the same fiction.

**V7 is the gate that proves determinism, and it is the only one that cannot prove
correctness.** It re-runs the same renderer on the same inputs. If assembly
cross-wires two units' responses - a file-handle reuse, an off-by-one in `part-NN`
offset concatenation - V7 reproduces the mistake byte-perfectly and reports
success. That is `mp4`'s job, not this one's, and a V7 that grows coverage it does
not have is a defect.

**Nine of the twelve gates in the spec were one line naming a check.** None
carried a threshold with provenance, none carried a failure behaviour, and none
carried a non-vacuity assertion. V7 is one of the ten that now does.

## Technical Approach
```
V7(receipts, vault_dir) :=
    for r in receipts:
        rendered = render(r)                       # the receipt is the ONLY input
        on_disk  = (vault_dir / r.relpath).read_bytes()
        FAIL if sha256(rendered) != sha256(on_disk)
        FAIL if rendered != on_disk                # byte-compare, not "close"
    NON_VACUOUS iff len(receipts) > 0
```
**Rendering from the vault compares the vault with itself and always passes.**
The receipt must be the only input.

**The `sha256` comparison and the byte-compare are both present and they are not
redundant.** SHA-256 of nothing equalled SHA-256 of nothing once, so a renderer
that produces nothing and a vault file that is absent both hash to the same value.
Assert `rendered` is non-empty before comparing hashes.

**`r.relpath` comes from `clean-names.json`,** not from the note's position on
disk. A relpath that does not resolve is a FAIL, not a skip - a receipt whose note
is missing is precisely the defect.

## Success Criteria
- Re-rendering from receipts reproduces every note byte-for-byte.
- A hand-edited note fails V7.
- A receipt with no corresponding note fails V7.

## Acceptance Criteria
**Reject a V7 unless it fails on these inputs:**

- Point `render` at the **note on disk** instead of the receipt -> the gate must
  refuse or fail. A reduction diff that tolerates whitespace, timestamp or ordering
  differences is not a reduction diff; it must be byte equality or it proves
  nothing.
- A hand-edited note -> FAIL on the byte-compare.
- A receipt whose `relpath` has no file -> FAIL.
- **An empty receipts list** -> FAIL, not PASS. `NON_VACUOUS iff len(receipts) > 0`.
- A renderer that returns a cached or empty value for a changed receipt -> FAIL.
  Plant a change in one receipt and assert the render output changes with it; a
  renderer that returns a constant passes an unchanged tree forever.
- **Exchange two units' `assembled.json` contents** -> V7 still PASSES, and it
  must. Reject an implementation that claims this as V7 coverage: it is `mp4`'s
  clause 4, and a V7 reduced to it has lost the property it was written for.

**Dependencies.** V7 is evaluated over the assembled tree (`a7z`) and re-renders
from receipts produced by `z72`. It runs before `dgu` in the egress sequence.

## Test Plan
- Unit: a hand-edited note -> FAIL on the byte-compare.
- Unit: a receipt whose `relpath` has no file -> FAIL.
- Unit: point `render` at the vault instead of the receipt -> the gate refuses.
- Unit: an empty receipts list -> FAIL, not PASS.
- Unit: change one receipt and assert the render output changes.
- E2E: re-render all 344 from receipts; assert byte equality.
- **Negative control:** exchange two units' `assembled.json` contents and assert
  V7 STILL PASSES. That is `mp4`'s defect, not V7's, and a V7 that fails it has
  over-reached.

## Considerations
- A reduction diff that tolerates whitespace, timestamp or ordering differences
  is not a reduction diff. It must be byte equality or it proves nothing.
- **This gate is expected to be UNEVALUABLE until the pipeline exists.** A
  specification is not an implementation; a gate is evaluable only once code
  exists that can fail it.
- The formula lives in `stage-1/stage-1-spec.md`. If the two disagree, the SPEC
  wins and this bead is wrong - that is the correct direction of disagreement.

title: V11 egress SHA256 per file
description:
## Background
The egress is the last chance to catch a corrupted or truncated copy. W0-Egress
proved `scp -r` is byte-exact: **4 of 4 files identical by SHA-256 across the
transfer, 0 mismatched, and 11 of 11 typography checks PASS after the copy**
(`-> × § ≥ ± ≈ ✓`, em dash, curly quotes, emoji, CJK, LF preserved, no BOM).
**Length is not integrity, and no shell pipeline touches the copy.**

**The corruption is real, and it lives in the two FORBIDDEN rewrites, not in the
transfer.** `Get-Content -Raw | Set-Content -Encoding utf8` and a `python -c`
heredoc both destroy non-ASCII. W0-Egress ships exactly that payload and measures
`scp -r` delivering it intact; the spec (§12) forbids those two rewrites **by
name** for that reason.

**Two figures this bead used to carry have no source and are withdrawn.**
`256 matched on length` and `11 of 11 spot-checks differed` appear nowhere in
`evidence/probes/nhbplus-w0-egress-2026-10-15.json`, which records
`"files": 4, "identical": 4, "mismatched": 0` and `"verdict": "PASS - 11 of 11"`.
No population of 256 or 267 files was ever transferred. **The spec's §11.4 V11
